articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Low-Loss Suspended Stripline Diplexer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized low-loss suspended stripline diplexer is presented. Firstly, we design two band-pass filters independently and then combine them using aT-junction to achieve an optimized collaborative diplexer. An elliptic function filter, featuring a series resonance circuit, introduces three transmission zeros (TZs) in the stopband, thereby enhancing the out-of-band rejection. The suspended stripline structure significantly reduces the profile and dielectric losses. Through simulation and measurement, we developed a suspended stripline low-pass filter (10 MHz - 2 GHz) and a high-pass filter (2 GHz - 4 GHz). By integrating these with a T-junction, we designed a broadband low-loss frequency diplexer covering the range from 10 MHz to 4 GHz. The diplexer exhibits an insertion loss lower than 1 dB across 95.37% of the passband.

articleTitle: A Low Phase Noise Switch-Less Dual Band VCO with Common Mode Resonance Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a CMOS-based voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) operating in both V and W bands by fully utilizing the harmonics in Class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\mathrm{F}_{23}$</tex> tank. The common mode (CM) resonance in Class- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{F}_{23}$</tex> tank is expanded via a transformer. It suppresses the flicker noise upconversion and improves the phase noise performance. This transformer also generates the 2nd harmonic output without switch. The measurement results show that the dual band VCO covers both 69.92 to 73.84 GHz and 104.88 to 110.75 GHz with a tuning range of 5.7%. The phase noise (PN) measured at 70 and 105 GHz is - 102.5 and −92.35 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset, with the corresponding figure-of-merit (FoM) being −182.5 and −176 dBc/Hz, respectively. In addition, the VCO consumes a power of 44 mW and occupies a relatively small silicon area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.36 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: 140 GHz Slow-Wave Structure Loaded SIW Miniaturized Butler Matrix for Multibeam Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a SIW Butler matrix loaded with slowwave structure is proposed for 140 GHz multi-beam applications. The Butler matrix is implemented in a single-layer quartz substrate. The phase delay part of the Butler matrix adopts periodically tapered “I”-shaped transverse slots, which shortens the y-axis dimension while keeping the x-axis dimension almost unchanged. This can achieve low loss, high compactness, and realize large-scale expansion of the Butler matrix.

articleTitle: Dual-Channel Millimeter Wave Field Strength Measurement System for High-Speed Maglev Train
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Based on the demand of field intensity measurement in MMwave vehicle-ground communication system of high-speed maglev train, a two-channel field intensity measurement system is designed in this paper. The system can achieve millimeter-level positioning accuracy, measure the two-channel receiving signal field strength at the same time, and verify the diversity effect of millimeter wave communication system. Compared with the traditional field strength measurement system, the system can realize the high-speed accurate measurement of the signal field strength in the millimeter wave band, and can meet the measurement requirements of large-scale scenarios such as high-speed maglev trains.

articleTitle: Tuner-based and F50 Measurement of HEMT Noise Parameters Determining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the tuner-based measurement and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{F}_{50}$</tex> method for characterizing four noise parameters of HEMT devices. General processes and requirements demanded for each method are introduced and compared. The noise parameters obtained by the two extraction methods shows similar results for 70 nm HEMT with 50 µm gatewidth in the frequency range 8-50GHz. The results indicate that both methods have their own advantages and disadvantages while maintaining accuracy. Based on the F50 noise parameter extraction method, an improvement direction has been proposed to reduce parameter extraction and optimize the process. Great usability is demonstrated for determination of noise parameters characterization.

articleTitle: A 70.6–98.4GHz Power Amplifier With Equivalent Low-K Matching Network and Slot-Balun-Based Power Combiner in 40-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a broadband power amplifier (PA) with wideband impedance matching techniques and slot-balun-based power combining. A high-coupling transformer with series inductor is proposed for inter-stage wideband matching, which functions as an equivalent lowcoupling (low-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>) matching network with additional design freedom. In addition, slot baluns are also introduced for wideband input/output impedance matching and power combining with low insertion loss, simultaneously. To verify the proposed design techniques, a prototype was implemented in a 40-nm LP CMOS process with a core area of 0.3Í0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The prototype achieves a 3-dB bandwidth from 70.6 GHz to 98.4 GHz, a maximum power gain of 20.6 dB, a saturated output power (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{sat}$</tex>) of 13.6 dBm, and a peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 10.5%.

articleTitle: Design of a Triple-Band and Ultra-Thin Absorber with Pixel Structure Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The pixel structure regards the design area as the binary matrix, which provides a promising view for the high-performance absorber design. This paper presents the design method for metamaterial absorber (MMA) with pixel structure based on proximal policy optimization (PPO), which is a reinforcement learning method. The triple-band and ultra-thin absorber with pixel structure is designed using the proposed method. Comparative study indicates that the PPO converges faster than the genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO). The absorption peak of the designed absorber occurs at 5.200 GHz, 14.425 GHz and 19.225GHz, respectively with ultra-thin profile.

articleTitle: Transformer-Feedback mm-Wave Injection-Locked Frequency Tripler with Enhanced Output Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a high-output-power injection-locked frequency tripler (ILFT) designed using 0.25-µm GaAs p-HEMT technology. Leveraging a transformer-based positive feedback network, an injection-current-boosting (ICB) transformer, and a high-order resonator, the proposed ILFT achieves a locking range (LR) of 4.59% from 22.12 to 23.16 GHz, while delivering an output power exceeding 9 dBm without the need for additional amplifier or buffer stages. Comprehensive EM simulations validate the design's effectiveness, making it a promising candidate for millimeter-wave communication and detection systems.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Transceiver Font-End with <2.5°/0.5-dB Phase/Gain Resolution, 11.8-dBm Psat and 10.2-dBm OP1 dB
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a four-element Ka-band transceiver (TRX) front end (FE) phased array chip in 65-nm CMOS technology. A phase shifter (PS) based on the transformer is employed to achieve superior phase resolution and compact chip area. The TRX gain control is achieved by a 6-bit 0.5-dB-step attenuator (ATT), which achieve an attenuation range of 31.5 dB. At the antenna interface, The implemented T/R switch (TRSW) based on transmission line is proposed to achieve low insertion loss and high isolation. By employing the technique, the TRSW achieves an minimum insertion loss of 0.1/0.4 dB in transmit (TX) and receive (RX) mode in 33–37 GHz. Experimental results demonstrate that the TX and RX paths achieve a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.625^{\circ}$</tex> phase resolution in the 33–37 GHz range with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{a} < 3.5^{\circ}$</tex> RMS phase error. The TRX FE also achieves a peak gain of −1 dB and a minimum noise figure (NF) of 3.8 dB in RX mode, as well as a peak gain of 6 dB and a maximum output 1-dB gain compressed point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{OP}_{1\ \text{dB}})$</tex> of 11 dBm in TX mode. The core area of the four-element chip is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.15\times 3.28\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Thermal Stress Effects on Quantum Transport in Gate-All-Around Nanosheet Field Effect Transistor in 3D Heterogeneously Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: 3D heterogeneous integration technology is a key approach to realize circuit/system miniaturization by high density integration of various radio frequency (RF) components/circuits, logic circuits, memories, sensors etc. However, the high integration density leads to high power consumption and further induces thermal stress which can affect performance and reliability of semiconductor devices. The thermal stress effects on gate-all-around nanosheet field effect transistor (GAA-NSFET) are simulated by self-consistently solving heat conduction equation, solid mechanics equilibrium equation, and quantum transport equations. The thermal stress and temperature are induced by self-heating of GAA-NSFET and RF high power devices, wherein the heat generation rate of GAA-NSFET is calculated by nonequilibrium Green's function with consideration of phonon scattering. Thermal stress affects quantum transport by changing band structure of channel material in GAA-NSFET, and temperature affects quantum transport by changing carrier Fermi-Dirac distribution and phonon dispersion in GAA-NSFET. The effects of thermal stress on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{D}-V_{G}$</tex> characteristics, effective capacitance, and delay time of GAA-NSFET are studied. Simulation results show the impact of thermal stress on GAA-NSFET varies for different channel crystal orientations.

articleTitle: Parametric Modeling of Hairpin-Line Microstrip Bandpass Filter using Pole-Zero-Based Neuro-TF Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a method combining neural network and transfer function based on pole-zero is used for parametric modeling of microwave passive devices. In this method, the electromagnetic(EM) response of the passive element is expressed as a pole-zero-gain transfer function of frequency. The relationship between pole-zero-gain and geometric variables is learned by the neural network. We alter the geometric parameters to get the training dataset and employ the MPVL algorithm to accurately compute the corresponding poles and zeros. This approach ensures that our training dataset captures a wide range of scenarios based on varying geometric configurations. However, the poles and zeros are not necessarily arranged in the same order each time. Therefore this paper uses the distance-based pole-zero matching method to solve the mismatch problem, which can improve the accuracy and robustness of the overall model. Finally, the model is verified by a hairpin-line microstrip bandnass filter.

articleTitle: A Review on Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transmission: Approaches and Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) is an emerging technology facilitating the concurrent transmission of information and power wirelessly. An overview of the fundamental concepts, recent advancements, and potential applications of SWIPT is provided. This work presents the key advantages and challenges of SWIPT, emphasizing its significance of SWIPT in the development of future wireless communication systems.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
Author Keywords: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: Research Progress of Silicon-Based V/E/W-Band Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Power amplifier is an integral part of millimeter-wave communication systems. Especially in the V/E/W band, when the amplifier operating frequency approximates the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\mathrm{T}/2}$</tex> of the silicon-based CMOS process, the substrate loss is significant, the active device gain is insufficient, and the passive device loss increases. Therefore, this paper summarizes several typical studies to improve silicon-based millimeter-wave power amplifiers efficiency, gain, and bandwidth performance. In particular, a gain boosting technique is proposed, and a prototype PA with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PAE_{\max}$</tex> of 22.37% and a gain of 26–31 dB is achieved in the E-band. In addition, owing to the proposed IEH-k transformer-based interstage matching network, a W-band PA with a single-path saturated output power of 13 dBm and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PAE_{\max}$</tex> of 21.1% is designed. Moreover, a V/E/W-band ultra-wideband PA covering a bandwidth of 67.8-108.2 GHz is realized in a 65nm CMOS technology based on the proposed novel TCL-CGB technique.

articleTitle: D-Band Beam Steering on Reconfigurable PB-Phase Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) are a pivotal technology in addressing terahertz beam tracking and aiming challenges for potential terahertz communication and imaging applications. To overcome the shortcomings of narrow bandwidth and poor reflectance consistency on conventional resonant phase-shift structure, this paper proposes a D-band RIS based on a Pancharatnam-Berry (PB)-phase mechanism. The PB-phase shift is delivered by the surface current reversal controlled by dual GaAs Schottky diodes in mirror placement, giving birth to improved 1-bit coding states with broadband width and consistent reflectance. Simulation results indicate that at a resonant frequency of 140 GHz, the structure achieves a maximum amplitude of approximately −3dB, a −7dB bandwidth spanning about 60 GHz, an accurate 180° phase shift, and a beam scanning range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 80^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 22^{\circ}$</tex>. The proposed PB-phase RIS paves a new path to terahertz beam steering and makes it promising for terahertz wireless communication and radar systems applications.

articleTitle: Simulation on Stacked Si Nanosheet nFETs with Dual-$k$ Spacers for Sub-2 nm-Node RF Applications (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work presents an NEGF -based modeling and simulation framework for the evaluation of parasitic effects and RF performance in stacked Si nanosheet nFETs at the sub-2 nm technology node. By comprehensively examining the figures-of-merit such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_{\mathrm{m}}, g_{d},f_{\mathrm{T}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\max}$</tex>, the roles of dual-k spacer, sheet width and crystal orientation are explored in the device design for potential RF and THz applications.

articleTitle: Miniaturized High-efficiency 5.8 GHz Rectifier Circuit for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposed a miniaturized high-efficiency 5.8 GHz rectifier for wireless power transfer (WPT). The rectifier adopts a simple single-diode parallel topology and achieves a simulated rectification efficiency of 74.2% at an input power of 13 dBm. However, due to fabrication errors, the measured rectification efficiency decreases to 43%. To address this issue, an improved rectifier is introduced. It replaces the distributed capacitance with DC blocks to reduce soldering errors, incorporates grounded via structures to reduce crosstalk between parallel microstrip lines, and chamfers the PCB edges to enhance board reliability. This updated design reduced the volume by 63.5% and increased the simulated efficiency to 77.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>• The updated rectifier has been fabricated and will be measured, which could be a prospective candidate for powering wireless sensor nodes.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an X-Band Limiter Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Based on the 0.15µm GaAs PHEMT process, a limiter low noise amplifier of 7-13GHz is designed and implemented in this paper. The circuit miniaturization is realized for the hybrid integrated circuit scheme and micro-assembly process, and the limiting power capacity and reliability of the circuit are improved for its balanced structure. The limiter low noise amplifier adopts a two-stage reverse parallel PIN diode structure to reduce insertion loss and improve circuit stability. A three-stage cascaded current reuse topology structure is used in the proposed low noise amplifier to guarantee the gain and reduce the power consumption of the circuit. On-wafer measured results show that the fabricated limiter low noise amplifier working frequency bandwidth is 7–13 GHz, the typical value of small signal gain is 29 dB, the noise figure is below 2.0 dB, 1 dB compressed point output power is higher than 11 dBm, the power resistance is greater than 20 W, and the chip size is 2.4mmx3.0mmx0.1mm.

articleTitle: Novel Spatial Three-Dimensional FSS with Elliptical Bandpass Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work presents a collection of novel three-dimensional (3-D) frequency selective surfaces (FSSs). Initially, we demonstrate that folded dipole resonators arranged in a mouth-to-mouth configuration facilitate the realization of second-order bandstop responses. Building upon this foundational design, we introduce cross-finger capacitors to enhance capacitive coupling between the dipole resonators. Subsequently, the implementation of a grounded metal wire on the backside generates spatial slot resonance, thereby achieving a high-selectivity second-order bandpass response. Leveraging these established structures, we advance the design by duplicating it into two elements, ultimately cul-minating in a third-order bandpass response characterized by quasi-elliptic filtering characteristics. The simplicity and fabrication ease of these designs make them suitable for a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Layout Automation for Analog and RF IC: Current Status and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of AI-enabled layout automation for analog and RF integrated circuits (ICs). We examine recent advancements in machine learning algorithms, optimization techniques, and AI-driven design methodologies tailored to the unique challenges of analog and RF IC layout. The paper highlights the benefits, limitations, and key achievements of these AI approaches and identifies existing gaps. Finally, we discuss future directions and research opportunities, emphasizing AI's potential to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of IC layout design.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-loaded Substrate-integrated Wave-guides in Sub-terahertz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) is noted for its low loss and ease of integration, being increasingly focused on developing terahertz circuits and systems. However, traditional SIWs face challenges in machining metal holes and frequency selection for the sub-terahertz band and beyond. To address these issues, this paper introduces a sub-terahertz metamaterial-loaded substrate-integrated waveguide (MLSIW). The proposed MLSIW incorporates rectangular split-ring resonators (RSRRs) with ro-bust shielding properties, replacing traditional SIW metal via holes to establish a virtual electric wall. A straight waveguide with a microstrip transition structure on a 1/30 wavelength thick quartz substrate is designed, featuring an operation frequency of 0.1 THz with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_11$</tex> less than -20 dB and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_21$</tex> greater than -1 dB, and 18.2% relative bandwidth. Moreover, a 90-degree bending wave-guide is designed with the RSRRs arranged in circular arcs, fea-turing an operation frequency of 0.1 THz with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_11$</tex> less than -30 dB, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_21$</tex> greater than -1 dB, and 15.5% relative bandwidth. This met-amaterial-Ioaded SIW presents advantages such as high integration, facile tuning, and simple stcucture. It is promising for evolving into reconfigurable circuits and components for highly inte-grated terahertz sensing, imaging, and communication systems. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{11}$</tex>

articleTitle: A Sub-Terahertz Balanced Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna Fed by an SRR-Loaded SIW Ridge Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The Vivaldi antenna, featured for its broadband capabilities, low profile, and high gain, has widespread application in the microwave frequency band. Aiming at the prevalent issues like significant transmission loss and gain limitations for the Vivaldi Antenna operating in the sub-terahertz regime, herein a balanced antipodal Vivaldi antenna based on a metamaterial-loaded substrate-integrated ridge waveguide excitation is designed. The antenna's feed section employs a substrate-integrated ridge waveguide loaded with tapered microstrip and split ring resonators (SRRs). The SRRs substitute the conventional metalised through-hole SIW, effectively enhancing high-frequency selectivity and mitigating processing complexity. The radiation section adopts a quadraticripple balanced antipodal structure, and adding a metallic director and a medium cavity significantly boosts the antenna's gain over 2 dBi. The antenna operates within the 95 GHz to 128 GHz range, with a return loss of less than −10 dB, a bandwidth of 29.6%, and a gain of 12.53 dBi. Characterised by its low cost, ease of integration, and enhanced radiation performance, this antenna holds promising prospects for application in 6G wireless communication and radar systems.

articleTitle: Design of D-Band power amplifier based on 0.13 um SiGe process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper introduces the design of a terahertz power amplifier chip with working frequency of 120–160 GHz based on 0.13 um SiGe process. The amplifier achieves high gain through the use of a differential cascode structure and a two-stage amplification structure. On-chip transformers are employed to design the input, output, and interstage matching circuits because the area is much smaller compared to microstrip line matching circuits. The accurate design of the terahertz power amplifier chip is realized through full-layout electromagnetic simulation. Simulation results indicate that the small-signal gain is 22 dB, the output 1 dB compression point is 10 dBm, and the power added efficiency is 6.2% at the center frequency of 140 GHz. The saturation power within the operating band is in the range of 9.7-11.9 dBm, and the 3 dB gain frequency range is from 128 GHz to 153 GHz.

articleTitle: A Rectenna Array with Wide-Coverage Beamforming and Polarization-Insensitive Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The advent of the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to the widespread use of wireless power transfer (WPT) systems, which are afflicted by three fundamental issues: limited coverage, polarization mismatch and uneven power. This paper proposes a rectenna array with wide coverage and polarization insensitivity, comprising a Nolen matrix, a dual-linearly polarized (DLP) antenna array, the hybrid coupler and a rectifier. The results of the measurements demonstrate that the rectenna array is effective in addressing the three issues previously identified, thereby rendering it suitable for radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting in WPT systems.

articleTitle: On-Chip Compact Surface Acoustic Wave Topological Delay Line Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) delay lines are widely used in RF signal processing, gyrometers and sensing, especially radar. Core devices in radar require simple and compact SAW delay lines. In traditional ones based on electroacoustic interdigital transducers, increasing delay time has limitations. Here, we present an on-chip SAW delay line using the bending immunity of the topological protected edge state. By folding the transmission path and modulating the SAW velocity, it can get large delay time in a compact structure. This work helps the application of advanced artificial materials in integrated devices.

articleTitle: Brillouin Fiber Laser for Differential Frequency Generation of Narrow Linewidth Terahertz Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper discusses the limitations of current electrical and optical methods of generating terahertz waves, introduces a Brillouin fiber laser for generating terahertz waves with narrow linewidth and analyzes its performance. The laser output wavelength tuning range of 18 nm can be achieved using C-band erbium-doped fibers as the gain medium. The laser can be used for differential frequency terahertz wave generation.

articleTitle: Ultra-narrow Band Microwave Photonic Filter Based on Brillouin Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate an ultra-narrow band microwave photonic filter based on single longitudinal mode parity time (PT) symmetry Brillouin fiber laser. The PT symmetry ensures the operation of single longitudinal mode laser, achieving an unusually narrow bandwidth of sub-kHz and high side mode suppression ratio. The MPF is achieved by combining a Brillouin fiber laser ring cavity with a PT symmetric system. By utilizing the loops and loss loops are formed in counterclockwise and clockwise directions, respectively. Then, we precisely adjust the polarization controller to achieve equal gain and loss for clockwise and counterclockwise light. The experimental results show that the 3dB bandwidth of MPF is approximately 72Hz, and the side mode suppression ratio is about 16.5dB.

articleTitle: 28-GHz WIPD Bandpass Filter with Wide-Stopband Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-miniaturized bandpass filter based on the WIPD technology. While maintaining small size, the bandpass filter was developed with four flexible transmission zeros (TZs) to attain high selectivity and wide stopband suppression. A third-order filter was prototyped and characterized. Measured minimum insertion loss and 3-dB bandwidth are 2.4 dB and 24.2%, respectively, for the center frequency at 26.5 GHz. Besides, the measured shape factor (i.e., BW_20dB/BW_3dB) is as low as 1.8. Over 10–50 GHz, four finite-frequency TZs contribute to a wide stopband range for greater than 19-dB suppression. The core size is 641 µm x 518 µm.

articleTitle: Integrated Dual-Band Microwave Resonant Sensor With Microfluidic Sorting Chip for Biological Cell Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Microwave biosensors are characterized by high sensitivity, real-time response, multi-parameter characterization, and low power consumption, which have a broad range of applications in the fields of food safety detection, environmental pollution monitoring, and biomedical healthcare. As microfluidic chips have the advantages of low sample volume, low cost and fast detection rate, the combination of microfluidic chips and sensor chips has practical applications in the biomedical field. The integrated microwave-microfluidic biosensor could enhance the sensitivity of the sensor, achieve high-throughput analysis of multiple or single samples, and provide a promising potential for the development of low-cost, compact microwave-microfluidic biosensors in multiple sensing applications. The microfluidic sorting chip for qualitative separation of mixed microorganism cells combined with microwave sensors for rapid detection solves the selectivity problem prevailing in current microwave biosensors.

articleTitle: Wideband Single-Pole Double-Throw Switch Based on Phase Change Material GeTe for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In our research, a broadband single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch based on germanium telluride (GeTe) which is suitable for millimeter-wave (mmWave) applications is presented. This switch consists of classical seven-layer structures. By introducing a bilayer dielectric barrier, the stage on the micro-heater is eliminated, which can realize planarization and improve the reliability of the device. Based on the above-mentioned planarization technology, the width of the micro-heater is designed to be narrower than that of the phase change gap for decreasing the coupling capacitance from the micro-heater. In simulation, the insertion loss of the SPDT switch is below 0.6dB and the isolation is above 12dB at 70GHz.

articleTitle: A W-Band Passive Phase Shifter with 0.42dB/1.9° RMS Magnitude/Phase Errors in 40nm CMOS (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a 75–95 GHz 6-bit passive phase shifter (PS) which consists of a compact quadrature generator circuit (QGC), a X-type attenuator, and a power combiner. A compact asymmetric power combiner (PC) based on T-bridge coil is used, leading to low-loss power combining and impedance matching with high isolation, simultaneously. Implemented in a TSMC 40-nm LP CMOS process, the proposed PS achieves a phase-shifting range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$360^{\circ}$</tex> with a phase step of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.625^{\circ}$</tex>. The measured root-mean-square (RMS) phase error is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.9^{\circ}-4.3^{\circ}$</tex> and the RMS gain error is 0.42-0.68 dB with zero DC power consumption. The core area of the proposed PS is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$550\times 280\text{um}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Ka-Band High-Linearity Attenuator with PVT Fluctuation Calibration for Temperature Compensation in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Applied in a Ka-band Multi-Channel Front-End to compensate for the gain drift caused by ambient temperature change, a temperature-controlled attenuator is designed in 65-nm CMOS process. Controlled by a Proportional to Absolute Temperature (PTAT) current that is built into the TR front-end chip, the attenuation amplitude shows a highly linear relationship with temperature. Benefiting from a feedback loop, it can generate a feedback voltage on devices to match port impedance automatically to 50 ohms, achieving low return loss below -15 dB over DC-40 GHz. Integrated with tuning circuit for process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) fluctuation calibration, negative effect caused by PVT can be minimized. Operating in a Ka-band front end, the attenuator achieves 7.5 dB gain compensation over - <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$55\sim 85^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Research Progress of Passive Attenuators ICs at Terahertz Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Attenuators are key modules for beamforming in millimeter-wave (mm-wave) wireless communication and radar systems. However, the increased switch losses at mm-wave frequencies, particularly in the D-band and above, result in higher overall insertion losses (IL). This paper presents two attenuator topologies applicable to mm-wave and terahertz (THz) regime. The proposed magnetically switchable coupled-lines (MSCL) based 4-bit attenuator achieves a minimum IL of 1.4 dB and an RMS amplitude error of < 0.34 dB operating from 190–220 GHz. To address the limited attenuation range of MSCL-based attenuator, a triple coupled resonant (TCR) based attenuator is proposed and provide a ~15 dB attenuation range with a minimum IL of 1.4 dB and RMS amplitude/phase errors of 0.3 dB and 1.7°, respectively.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Simulation of Hybrid Bonding Process-Induced Stress Effects on Quantum Transport in p-Type FinFET in Integrated Chiplets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Hybrid bonding plays an important role in advanced 2.5D/3D integrated chips due to its distinctive advantages such as higher interconnect density, lower power consumption, and better signal integrity. However, the performance of the logic device in chiplets can be affected by the strain induced by the annealing and cooling steps of hybrid bonding. The impact of hybrid bonding process on performance of FinFET is theoretically investigated by introducing stress from hybrid bonding process into quantum transport simulation for FinFET based on NEGF formalism, in which the impact of hybrid bonding process-induced stress on band structure is captured by employing six-band <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> Hamiltonian and deformation potential theory. According to simulation results, due to the hybrid bonding process-induced stress, the Y parameters operated at 100GHz and the on-state current can be enhanced.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Gain Millimeter-Wave MUTC Photodiode Integrated Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband high-gain millimeter-wave photonically driven radiator, which consists of a unitraveling carrier photodiode (MUTC-PD) powered vivaldi antenna. The vivaldi antenna gain is enhanced by loading with an elliptical patch. The results illustrate that the antenna covers a wide bandwidth of 12-28.5 GHz and peak gain of 9 dBi with minimized cross-polarization level of −20 dB. The proposed antenna is a promising candidate for low-cost millimeter-wave wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Campact GaN Dual-band SPDT Switch with Coupled Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band GaN MMIC SPDT switch design. Utilizing a novel on-chip coupled-line (OCL) topology, the input signal can be directed into either low- or high-band paths, thereby achieving dual-band characteristics. The operating frequencies for the low- and high-bands are determined by carefully selecting the electrical lengths of the OCLs and the device size for the corresponding shunt-FETs. This design approach results in improved insertion loss (IL) and isolation (ISO) within a compact structure. With the proposed techniques, an SPDT circuit has been fabricated in a 0.25-µm GaN-on-SiC process. The SPDT consists of a low-band path and a high-band path, achieving an average IL/ISO of 1.0/32 dB with the best input 1-dB compression points (IP1dB) of 37.2 dBm in the low-band of DC-15 GHz, and an average IL/ISO of 2.0/28.5 dB with the best IP/dB of 32.8 dBm in the high-band of 20–40 GHz. Additionally, the return loss is better than 11 dB for each port.

articleTitle: A SHA-Less 14-bit 500-MS/s Pipeline ADC in 28-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this parper, a SHA-less 14-bit 500MS/s pipeline analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is described. The thin-oxide MOSFETs are properly used to make full use of the high-speed characteristics of nanoscale CMOS devices while overcoming the negative impact, such as limited intrinsic gain and voltage margin. Also, current reuse techniques are used to design power-efficient input/reference buffers and opamps. The proposed pipeline ADC achieves a SNR of 70.5dB and a SFDR of 85.5dBc with a 243-MHz input sampled at the rate of 500MS/s, while consuming 550 mW power, and occupying an area of 1.45 mm2 in a 28nm CMOS.

articleTitle: A W-Band High-Gain Differential LNA Using Cross-Coupled Neutralization Capacitors in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a W-band low noise amplifier (LNA) fabricated in 65-nm CMOS. The LNA is composed of a four-stage differential common-source cascade structure and utilizes the cross-coupled neutralization capacitors to maximize the power gain. Measurement results shows that the proposed LNA exhibits a peak gain of 22 dB at 90 GHz with 10 GHz 3 dB bandwidth. The minimum noise figure of 8.4 dB is obtained at 94 GHz. The proposed LNA consumes a power of 56 mW with 1 V dc supply and the total chip area, including the pads, is 0.636 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It is designed to realize high-integration, high-reliability, and high-power RF front-end.

articleTitle: A High-Power-Density Synchronous GaN Class-F Rectifier MMIC for On-Chip MWPT Micro-System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a fully integrated syn-chronous class-F rectifier monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) using GaN HEMT technology. The design is based on the time-reversed dual of the corresponding class-F power amplifier (PA). Up to 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonics are controlled for not only the efficiency enhancement but also the fundamental impedance matching. With the proposed method, the rectifier size is controlled as 1.02 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the rectification power density is up to 2598 kW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The maximum drain efficiency (DE) of the proposed class-F PA is 65.4% at 10 GHz, and the RF-DC efficiency is 65.2% with a 205 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex> load. With low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology, the proposed synchronous rectifier can be integrated into the receiver of a minimized on-chip microwave wireless power transfer (MWPT) micro-system.

articleTitle: Constant-Current-Output and High-Efficiency Class E Inverter with Wide-Range Load
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: wireless charging always suffers efficiency degradation from load variation, which seriously constrains its wide application. In this research, a T-match network is introduced in Class-E inverter to achieve high efficiency by compressing wide-range equivalent impendence from load variations. In the meantime, optimization of capacitors among the T-match is conducted to maintain constant current output. In Advanced Design System(ADS), The improved Class E with T-match at 6.78MHz achieve power output ranging from 10 to 45 W, a constant current output of 1.4 A, and a transmission efficiency exceeding 85% under load variations from 10Ω to 50 Ω in the experiment.

articleTitle: Compact IoT Wireless Charging System with Impedance Matching Elimination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band metasurface-structured antenna is designed to eliminate the need for a complex impedance matching network. The antenna excites the fundamental TM10 and higher-order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TM}_{20}$</tex> modes, operating at 2.1 GHz and 2.45 GHz, respectively. Integrating the rectifier circuit, the rectenna demonstrates the peak RF-to-DC conversion efficiencies of 60.1% at 2.1 GHz and 60% at 2.45 GHz. The most significant advantage of this design is eliminating the complex impedance matching network, resulting in a compact, simple, cost-effective and high-efficiency rectenna. The major contribution lies in exploring how metasurface antenna parameters influence the real and imaginary parts of impedance matching. This type of antenna is particularly suitable for low-power sensor charging applications like forest fire monitoring and medical devices powering. Measurement results closely match the simulation results, validating the effectiveness of the design.

articleTitle: Characterization and Extraction Method Study on MOSFET Threshold Voltage DIBL Effects from 300 K Down to 10 K
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: With growing interest in cryo-CMOS for quantum computing, this study systematically evaluates the suitability of various <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{th}$</tex> extraction methods across a temperature range from 300 K down to 10 K with Drain-Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL) effects. For the first time, the square root <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{d}$</tex> (SQ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{d}$</tex>) method is proposed for optimal extrapolation based on characterization data collected from both commercial 180-nm and 40-nm bulk MOSFETs, respectively.

articleTitle: A Compact Class-F Broadband-Harmonic-Shaping VCO for Mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a compact Class-F voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) for mm-Wave applications such as radar and 5G mm-Wave communication. An on-chip T-Type 8-Shaped transformer is proposed to achieve broadband differential mode (DM) impedance at the third harmonic, allowing the VCO to operate in Class-F state without additional harmonic tuning. The VCO was designed in TSMC 40nm CMOS LP process and the proposed 8-Shaped transformer is laid out by stacking under the resonant transformer, with a compact core area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.042 \text{mm}^2$</tex>. The post-simulation results show that the VCO covers the frequency range of 24.6-26.8 GHz, achieving a phase noise (PN) of −111 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset, corresponding to a FOM and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{FOM}_{\mathrm{A}}$</tex> value of 190 dBc/Hz and 204 dBc/Hz respectively.

articleTitle: All Optical Microwave Oscillator Based on Forward Brillouin Radial Acoustic Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: An all optical microwave oscillator based on Forward Brillouin radial acoustic mode is proposed. The oscillator consists of two loops, with a main loop of 5 km SMF and a sub loop of 300 m SMF. Through the vernier effect, it achieves single longitudinal mode (SLM) output based on forward brillouin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}_{0,7}$</tex> acoustic mode. The threshold power is 300 mW, and the sound mode and longitudinal mode suppression ratios are 28.76 dB and 39.13 dB, respectively. This study has enormous potential in fields such as optical communication and optical sensing.

articleTitle: An Interdigital Capacitor Based Differential Microwave Sensor for Solid Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel differential design consisting of three interdigital capacitor structure to improve sensitivity and avoid environment interference. The frequency shift of the designed sensor was first simulated and then measured by locating materials with different dielectric constants. Region 1 was verified as the most sensitive area to distinguish different solid materials, and the sensor exhibits the ability to estimate defects on surface. The measured results also confirm its potential in thickness and loss tangent detection.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Array Antenna With Wide Range Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The study of scanning antenna arrays with multipolarization is of great value in improving the transmission rate of communication systems. In this paper, a small-scale dualpolarized magneto-electric dipole phased array is proposed to excite two orthogonal line-polarized radiation patterns by using two orthogonal L-shaped metal patches to de-excite the magnetoelectric dipole antenna. The port isolation of both polarizations is below -25 dB in the range of 24.25-27.5 GHz.A 4 × 4 phased array is constructed based on the proposed magneto-electric dipole antenna, with the array size less than 2λ0 × 2λ0 × 0.2λ0.In order to reduce the mutual coupling between the antenna units, a metal cylindrical array is added around the antenna to suppress the transmission of surface waves. Finally, the proposed antenna array can achieve ±50° dual-polarized beam scanning.

articleTitle: A K-Band Common Source Low Noise Amplifier in 0.15-µm GaN/SiC HEMT Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a GaN HEMT designed LNA with WIN 0. 15um process for 18–27 GHz (K-band) is presented. The LNA adopts a four-stage common-source structure to achieve 22.8-24.8dB gain in the full K-band. In order to reduce noise and improve matching, the core amplifier adopts a source-simplex inductor structure, which realizes a noise figure of 1.9-2.4dB in the operating band and stable operation in the full frequency band. The LNA chip area is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.37\times 0.96\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: An Exponential Curvature-Compensate Bandgap Voltage Reference with Enhanced Power Supply Rejection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a low quiescent current (IQ), low temperature coefficient (TC), high power supply rejection (PSR) bandgap voltage reference (BGR) for low dropout regulators (LDO) is proposed. Innovations are made based on the traditional bandgap voltage reference by introducing a zero-power start up circuit, a PSR enhancement structure and an exponential curvature-compensation structure. The BGR is designed using SMIC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> BCD process. Simulation results show that at supply voltages ranging from 3V to 5V, the quiescent current is 27.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex>, the reference voltage is 1.206V, the TC is 4.99 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ppm}/^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, and the linear regulation ratio is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$198.6 \mu \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{V}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Back Propagation Algorithm-Driven Design Method of Cantilever Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Cantilever beam is a widely used structure in a highly sensitive sensor towards various applications, while designing an appropriate structure that meet multiple constraints is time-consuming. In this paper, a method of cantilever beam structure design with a resonance frequency of 100 Hz driven by back propagation(BP) algorithm is demonstrated, which will greatly improve efficiency and accuracy of sensor design. A three-layer neural network with 10 hidden neurons cantilever beam design model was created, after 200 epochs training, the mean squared error(MSE) and mean absolute percentage error(MAPE) of the neural network were 0.148828 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.46051\times 10^{-5}$</tex>. Moreover, the feasibility and accuracy of cantilever beam structure design driven by the BP algorithm is verified, the resonance frequency of 100.06Hz cantilever beam was designed with absolute percentage error of 0.069%.

articleTitle: The DC and RF Performance by Fe Doping Tail of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with Different GaN channel layer thicknesses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this work, the effects of Fe doping tails on gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with different GaN channel layer thicknesses were systematically investigated, including DC and RF performance. The unintentionally doped (UID) GaN channel layer thicknesses prepared in this article were 650 nm and 200 nm, respectively. It has found that HEMT with a 200 nm channel layer has a lower leakage current of 276.×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> and a higher breakdown voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{BR}$</tex>) of 187 V. However, due to the thinner channel layer, the concentration of Fe doping tails reaching at the 2DEG at the AlGaN/GaN interface is higher, which enhances scattering and reduces mobility, resulting in more severe current collapse and slightly lower RF performance. Therefore, it is crucial to choose the appropriate UID GaN channel layer thickness for different applications.

articleTitle: A High-Power-Density Stacked CMOS Power Amplifier Using a Triple-Coil Interweaved Parallel Combining Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This brief presents a high-power-density amplifier utilizing a compact triple-coil interweaved parallel combining transformer (TIPC) and a modified low-loss three-way parallel power splitter for transformation from single-ended to triple-ended (S3D) in the 0.13-µm CMOS SOI process. The power am-plifier (PA) is based on a differential three-stack-transistor (TST) configuration, a ladder-type interconnection method and the RC feedback technique to reduce reflection loss and balance maximum available gain and stability. And the PA utilizes an improved zero-degree combiner (ZDC) with high-quality factor (Q-factor) metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors and well-designed pattern ground to reduce the loss of passive matching networks. Therefore, the silicon-based P A shows a competitive power density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.319 \mathrm{W}/\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. Simulated results demonstrate that this PA exhibits a peak gain of 18.3 dB at 7.1 GHz and a 50% bandwidth from 6 to 10 GHz. Due to the proposed three-way splitter and TIPC combiner, the PA achieves a power-added efficiency (PAE) of 38.4%, saturation output power (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P}_\text{SAT}$</tex>) up to 28.2 dBm within a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.501 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Highly Integrated Multi-Channel Receiver for X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a highly integrated multi-channel receiver for X band applications. This receiver adopts system-in-package (SIP) RF Front-end and SIP to board level integration, achieving highly miniaturization and lightweight. With co-simulation of field and circuit, this multi-channel receiver is designed and developed. The results show that the gain of the multi-channel receiver is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40+2\text{dB}$</tex>, the noise factor (NF) is better than 6dB, and the isolation between different channels is superior to 50dB. This method can be extended and applied to S to Ka band.

articleTitle: An 135GHz Direct-Digital 16-QAM Modulator in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work presents an 135GHz direct-digital 16QAM modulator with independent amplitude and phase modulation. The modulator, implemented in 28nm CMOS, requires an 135 GHz local oscillator signal with a power level of 3 dBm and the peak output power is -3dBm. The total DC power consumption of the 16-QAM is 50mW, with a maximum data rate of 21 Gb/s, while maintaining EVM below -22.8dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Microwave Sensor for Traditional Chinese Medicine Decoctions Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a high-sensitivity substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) microwave sensor for traditional Chinese medicine decoctions detection. The designed microwave sensor is based on elliptical electric-LC(EELC) and interdigital capacitors (IDC). The regent under test (RUT) with different permittivities from 2 to 5 and dimensions of 9 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 11$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 0.8$</tex> mm is placed on the sensitive area of the sensor. According to the simulated result, the resonant frequency of the sensor shifts between 4.06 and 5.63 GHz with the variation of the RUT permittivity. The designed sensor can achieve sensitivity up to 8.28%, which shows a good feasibility in detecting liquid dielectric properties.

articleTitle: Anti-reverse Burning Design of LNA in High-power TR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In high-power microwave TR front-end applications, to prevent power leakage from the transmitter from burning out the low-noise amplifier (LNA) at the receiving channel front-end, isolators and limiters are designed at the input of the LNA. As the module size decreases, the transmitter may also leak to the output of the LNA through coupling and other means in a narrow space, causing reverse burning of the LNA. This manuscript elaborates on the design of LNAs for anti-reverse burning in high-power TR front-end from two aspects. Firstly, in terms of the front-end structure design of TR, a stage isolator is added at the output of the LNA to isolate the reverse input power to improve the chip's ability to resist reverse power; Due to the need to consider the noise coefficient of the system, the isolator can't provide sufficient isolation, The LNA itself needs to consider the ability to resist reverse burning. This manuscript analyzes this for the first time and points out the influence of processing technology and transistor size on the ability to resist reverse burning.

articleTitle: A W-band Amplifier in 0.1 µm GaAs pHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a three-stage driver amplifier designed using WIN Semiconductor's 0.1 µm GaAs technology, delivering low ripple, wide bandwidth, and high power capabilities within the frequency range of 81 to 103 GHz. High-order, low-loss L-shaped matching networks are employed for input and output matching to extend the bandwidth. Experimental results demonstrate a peak gain of 12 dB at 90 GHz, accompanied by a relative 3-dB bandwidth of 23.9% (81–103 GHz). Within this frequency range, the amplifier exhibits a saturated output power exceeding 14 dBm, with a maximum measured value of 17.4 dBm at 94 GHz. Operating at 4 V, the amplifier draws a current of 122 mA, resulting in a power consumption of 488 mW. Its core area is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.35\times 0.9\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. inclusive of pads.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a DC - 20 GHz Ultra Broadband Distributed Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Based on the distributed amplifier theory, an ultra-broadband low noise amplifier was designed in 0.15 um GaAs pHEMT technology. The amplifier adopted nine-stage cascade topology, which was composed of a common source structure and a common gate structure, and the chip area was 3.0 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 1.5$</tex> mm. The amplifier showed that the gain was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(20\pm 0.2)\ \text{dB}$</tex>, the input return loss was less than -17 dB, the output return loss was less than -19 dB, the output power at 1 dB gain compression was more than 20 dBm, the saturated output power was from 24.7 to 25.7 dBm and the noise figure was less than 3 dB over the frequency band from DC to 20 GHz.

articleTitle: Spiral Inductor ANN Scalable Model for 0.1um GaAs pHEMT Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work achieves a scalable inductor model based on the 0.1um GaAs RF process. The values of the components in the modified single-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> equivalent circuit were extracted from the data obtained through large-scale EM simulations, where the EM simulation results were calibrated by the full-wafer measurement results to ensure accuracy. The model scalable process is implemented by an artificial neural network. With the geometric size parameters as the input layer and the values of the equivalent circuit components as the output layer, a neural network model was established to characterize the nonlinear relationship between them, thereby expanding the effective range of the model. This scalable inductor model maintains good agreement with the EM data within the 110GHz range. By packaging this model into the PDK, it lays the groundwork for improving the efficiency of circuit design.

articleTitle: Broadband Low-profile Antenna with Nonuniform Metasurface for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a planar antenna with integrated nonuniform metasurface for broadband miniaturization is proposed, which is suitable for 5G applications. The proposed nonuniform metasurface consists of eight open-loop units, half of which are equipped with a T-patch and the other half are cleverly extended towards the center to form an angular patch to excite an additional third resonant mode. This design significantly enhances the antenna's working bandwidth, providing better coverage of the 5G spectrum and meeting the requirements of next-generation communication technology. The metasurface is directly integrated on the substrate where the antenna is located, which not only simplifies the manufacturing process, but also allows the antenna height to be only 0.18λ0. The simulation results indicate that the antenna's 10 dB impedance bandwidth is 79.8% within the frequency range of 2.16 to 5.03 GHz. The isolation between ports exceeds 20.9 dB. The antenna achieves a maximum gain of 11.2 dBi at 4.2 GHz, demonstrating excellent radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement for Wideband Dipole Antenna Array Utilizing Parasitic Decoupling Element
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband dipole antenna array with a parasitic decoupling element is presented. The antenna elements are E-plane arranged. By introducing the parasitic decoupling element between two antenna elements, multicoupling cancellation between neighboring antenna elements can be achieved to produce a high port isolation level of the antenna array. The parasitic decoupling element consists of a bent metal strip, which is printed on a vertically placed substrate and a bent metal strip. To evaluate the efficacy of the proposed self-decoupling method, a 1 × 2 antenna array is simulated. The results reveal the degree of isolation between the two antenna elements exceeds 25 dB over the entire operating bandwidth (where |S11|<-10 dB), while the port isolation level of the counterpart array is about 15 dB.

articleTitle: A V-Band High Linearity Down-Conversion Mixer Using Distributed Derivative Superposition Technique in 90-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A V-band high linearity down-conversion mixer in 90-nm CMOS is presented in this paper. The mixer utilizes the distributed derivative superposition (DS) linearization technique to achieve high linearity with relatively low power consumption. Furthermore, the active load is used to improve conversion gain and linearity. The mixer achieves a 2dBm IP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>, and the IIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is 15.2dBm. The measured conversion gain is -4.8dB with a 3dB bandwidth that covers from 47GHz to 62GHz. The mixer consumes only 12mW dc power with a chip area of 0.71mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>

articleTitle: Study on Primary Standard Calibration Type-N Thermistor Mount at 1 0 MHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: To accurately measure the power meter output voltage when calibrating the effective efficiency of a Type-N thermistor mount using the NIM primary standard at 10 MHz, we propose connecting the voltmeter at the isolated end of the power meter. The NIM-IV power meter is used to connect a thermistor mount for DC substitution, with the substitution power calculated by measuring the power meter output voltage using a voltmeter connected to the voltage terminal of the power meter. For calibration at 10 MHz, due to leakage, the thermopile output behaves differently when the power meter output voltage is measured using 34420A and 34401A, respectively, resulting in different calculated effective efficiencies. We propose connecting a voltmeter at the isolated end of the power meter to measure the power meter output voltage without affecting the measurement results, greatly ensuring the accuracy of the primary standard calibration at 10 MHz.

articleTitle: A Wideband and Low-Phase-Noise Dual-Core Triple-Mode VCO with Auxiliary Magnetic Loop in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A dual-core triple-mode voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) is proposed in this work, which uses the magnetic coupling between the auxiliary inductor and the main inductor to realize the resonant mode extension and further improve the tuning range (TR). Octagonal tail inductors with high quality factor (Q) are added at the tail of the resonator to form a high-impedance node at second harmonic. It inhibits the injecting of power supply noise into the resonator and weakens the Q-loading of the resonator when the transistors enter linear region, thus improving the phase noise (PN) performance. The proposed VCO is implemented in TSMC 65nm CMOS process. The post-simulation results show that the VCO has a wide frequency tuning range from 17.49 to 34.13 GHz, and the DC power consumption under 0.6 V power supply is only 11.66mW. The best phase noise at 1MHz is −112.6 dBc/Hz at 17.5 GHz, and the best figure of merit (FoM) value is 189 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: A C-Band Performance-Enhanced FBAR Filter with Integrated Adjustable Inductors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work presents a performance-enhanced acoustic wave filter with wafer-level packaging (WLP) by integrating adjustable matching inductors. The three-dimensional (3D) spiral inductors are designed for the impedance match of the acoustic filter chip. The inductance value can be continuously adjusted by selecting the different bonding position of the bond wires on the inductor, so the filtering performance of the acoustic wave filter can be enhanced greatly. A C-band film bulk acoustic resonator (FBAR) filter with a compact 3D spiral inductor with an inductance of 2.1 nH at 1 GHz and a maximum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> factor of 49.5 has been designed and implemented on the multilayered packaging substrate. The simulation results show that the proposed FBAR filter can obtain a better in-band response. According to the test results, the in-band ripple of the FBAR filter with a center frequency of 5.9 GHz reduces from 1.3 dB to 0.15 dB comparing to the FBAR filter without the inductors, while the insertion loss reduces 1.6 dB. The performance-enhanced WLP FBAR filter can be used in the RF front-end module (FEM) for mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: A New Coding Scheme of a 2-Bit Amplitude Controlling Leaky-Wave Antenna for Generating Switchable Cosecant-Squared Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, the traditional leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) are simplified as a 2-bit uniform one-dimension (1-D) antenna array used for calculating radiation pattern of antenna. For this antenna array, the amplitude of elements can be set as 0, 1, 2 or 3. To generate cosecant-squared radiation pattern, new coding scheme split the 2-bit antenna array into three 1-bit antenna arrays and calculates states of different 1-bit antenna arrays. By adjusting gain and radiation angle of different beams of 1-bit antenna arrays, the three beams form into one beam with cosecant-squared radiation angle. To verify the proposed coding scheme, states of elements of eight cosecant-squared beams with different radiation angle are calculated. The corresponding electric field is calculated and shown. From the calculated results, the simulated cosecant-squared radiation patterns are close with the ideal cosecant-squared radiation patterns, which reveals advantage of proposed antenna array.

articleTitle: Simple Single-Layer Miniaturized Filtenna Based on Multiple Shorted Patches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a single-layer miniaturized filtenna with a simple structure and compact size is developed. The developed antenna incorporates both a driven patch and a proximity patch, both of which are shorted patches that contribute to reducing the size of the antenna. A new resonance point and a radiation null are obtained by loading the U-slot. The resonant frequency of the driven patch is significantly lower than that of the U-slot due to their size relationship. To address this issue, four pairs of shorted pins are added to the driven patch to increase its resonant frequency, aligning it more closely with that of the U-slot. This adjustment results in a wider impedance bandwidth (IBW) for improved overall performance. Then, a radiation null and a resonance point are generated using proximity patch, which improves the IBW and out-of-band rejection in the upper stop-band. The designed single-layer miniaturized filtenna achieves a -to-dB IBW of 8.8% and keeping a profile of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.017\lambda_{0}$</tex>. In addition, the antenna has good out-of-band rejection performance.

articleTitle: High Performance LNA Integration for Advanced RFFE Module SoC Applications in 65nm SOI Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A 1.2V thin PD SOI FB NMOS devices is optimized with channel length of 55nm achieves peak Ft of>180GHz, ft of 100GHz, NFmin of<0.2dB@5GHz, gain of>28dB@1GHz at Gm/Ids=10S/A which can cover LNA design across sub-8GHz bands sufficiently. Passive devices are integrated with quality factor of >31 inductor and >43 MIM capacitor at sub-8GHz in HR trap rich SOI substrate with optimized BEOL. Design of a low power full integrated cascode LNA with power and gain control at 2.5GHz is implemented with gain of 21.5dB, NF of 0.78dB and good FOM of 10.6GHz demonstrate great potential of high performance LNA integration for advanced RFFE module SoC applications in 65nm SOI technology.

articleTitle: A 0-62.50-MHz Configurable Multi-Segment DDFS Chirp Generator for Integrated Satellite Radar Applications in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a DDFS digital control module driving an 8-16GHz numerically controlled variable frequency phase-locked loop (PLL). The module utilizes a top-level state machine configuration and control mechanism along with an internal pipeline structure for signal conversion and output, which ensures continuous phase, rapid system response time, and flexible configuration capabilities. By employing data compression and switchable phase dithering techniques, we achieved a spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of at least 95.71 dBc and a frequency flatness of up to 2.83 dB within the operating band, ensuring high signal quality. Additionally, the system can flexibly output chirp signals in various organizational forms and, through the DAC module, serve as the excitation frequency for the PLL module, thereby achieving frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) signal synthesis.

articleTitle: Design of a Frequency Conversion Front End Based on SIP
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this article, a broadband frequency conversion front end covers from 6 GHz to 18GHz, based on System in Package (SIP) is fabricated. The gain of the whole module is about 20dB, with the noise figure about 6dB, which can be used as the front end of the frequency conversion module. The designed works of this RF front end module contains a MEMS filter group, a Low noise amplifier, a digital attenuation with maximum attenuation up to 31.5 dB, temperature compensated attenuator and an equalizer. The whole module is designed based on ceramic ball grid array (CBGA) package. At last, the result is tested by a test fixture and the results meet the proposed target well. What's more the whole size of the module is about 16mm × 11mm × 3.1 mm, which is only 1/8 of the original discrete devices.

articleTitle: An Active EMI Filter Based on Midpoint Current Detection Used in Motor Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper analyzes and designs a common-mode (CM) active filter (CM-AEF) based on neutral point current detection for suppressing electromagnetic interference (EMI) in motor drive systems. It takes the neutral point of the DC side of the tested equipment as the reference point and uses a shunt resistor circuit to detect the CM current. An operational amplifier is used to form a current source circuit to generate compensating current. Compared with traditional current detection active filters, this filter does not require the use of a transformer and does not need noise separation, thus further reducing the volume of the active filter. The working principle of the filter is first analyzed, and then experimental verification is conducted. The experimental results show that the designed AEF has good attenuation capability for CM EMI in the frequency band of 150 kHz to 30 MHz.

articleTitle: 90 GHz Analog Kramers-Kronig Direct Detection Receiver in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article introduces a W-band synthesizer-free analog Kramers-Kronig (KK) coherent receiver, achieving QAM recovery at 200 Mbps with a EVM of −18 dB. The design is focused on direct detection, eliminates the need for LO generation, significantly reducing circuit complexity and DC power consumption to 34.8 mW, all within a compact 0.132 mm-size. This design and implementation of the integrated coherent receiver exploits the well known KK relationship with approximated non-linear circuit blocks to avoid bandwidth expansion while minimizing signal-to-signal interference, resulting in 1.8 dB improvement in EVM and a 0.8 dB reduction in CSPR compared to traditional direct detection methods. To the best of authors' knowledge, this is the first fully integrated analog mixed-signal implementation of KK receiver, establishing new standards in high-frequency communication systems.

articleTitle: A High Gain Wideband Amplifying Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper shows a X-band polarization conversion amplifying metasurface. The unit of the metasurface consists an aperture-coupled patch antenna, a BJT with bias network and a power amplifier chip. The metasurface has the characteristics of wideband, high polarization conversion rate and high gain of signal amplification. Compared with the traditional metasurface, the power of the transmitted signal is significantly increased. After using ADS and CST co-simulation, the two results agree well. The gain of the metasurface in 7.7∼9.7GHz is greater than 0dB, in 8∼9.5GHz is higher than 10dB and in 8.7∼9.4GHz, the gain is even more than 20dB.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Parametric Modeling of Microstrip Structures: Combing Neural Networks and RLGC-Based Eigenfunctions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article introduces an innovative electromagnetic (EM) parametric modeling approach that integrates neural networks with eigenfunctions based on circuit element (RLGC) for microstrip configurations. Previously, neural networks are employed to ascertain the undisclosed correlation between the RLGC parameters of geometrical parameters and the eigen-function. The creation of training data relies on accurately determining the eigenvalues of various modes. Nevertheless, the inconsistency between the modes and computable eigenvalues leads to the mode swapping problem. To address this challenge, we introduce a mode-matching approach based on eigenvectors.
