Once the training data is acquired, we suggest an initial training phase for the neural networks, followed by a two-step refinement training process for the neuro-EF model, to establish the comprehensive EM parametric model. Through this modeling approach, the trained model demonstrates swift and precise forecasting of EM responses as geometrical parameters undergo alterations in two-port microstrip configurations. In the realm of parametric modeling for microstrip structures, our proposed technique achieves enhanced accuracy across broader geometrical variations compared to existing methodologies. To elucidate the proposed method, we present one example of microstrip structures.

articleTitle: Nanoplasma Devices for Terahertz Applications: Performance Simulation and Optimization (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Nanoplasma devices, as a novel type of device that breaks the fundamental power-frequency trade-off limitation in traditional electronics, have paved the way for generating and amplifying terahertz signals. However, as an emerging device, existing nanoplasma devices often face challenges such as limited lifetime and lack of simulations for high frequency characterization. In this study, we have realized nanoplasma devices using the IC-compatible process. While maintaining the characteristics of the nanoplasma devices, we have decreased the gap size, improved the electrode material, and increased the electrode thickness, ultimately enhancing the device's operational lifetime. Moreover, we have simulated the wave emission simulations for the generation of terahertz signals of the nanoplasma device integrated with a bowtie antenna as the switch using CST simulations.

articleTitle: Negative Coupling Realized by Groove Gap Waveguide (GGW) and its Application for a CQ Waveguide Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Negative coupling is widely used in microwave filter design, especially for filters with finite transmission zeros (TZs). Conventionally, negative coupling is physically realized by capacitive irises or electrical probes. When negative coupling is small, the capacitive iris size usually becomes very small or the electrical probes need to be carefully placed, the manufacturing and tuning of filters, as a consequence, is of great challenge. In this paper, a coupling structure based on groove gap waveguide (GGW) is proposed to implement negative coupling and applied to a cascaded quadruplet (CQ) waveguide filter. The simulated and measured results demonstrate that the GGW coupling structure can perfectly replace the capacitive iris to implement the desirable negative coupling while favorably easing manufacturing difficulties caused by small negative couplings and lowering sensitivity to manufacturing tolerance for waveguide filters.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Reconfigurable Reflectarray Element with Arbitrary Polarization based on Liquid Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A ultra-small size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0.215\lambda_{0})$</tex> reflectarray element is designed using liquid crystal (LC) for tuning reflection phase. The element structure is made up of a rotationally symmetric and complicated metal patch mounting on the LC substrate, which supporting the arbitrary polarization. The metal patch consists of a hollow swastika patch, a square loop, a narrow stripline connecting the two parts together, and a meander stripline conducting the reflectarray elements as the DC ground. All of them generate three successive resonant modes, resulting in the broad operating band. The simulated results show that the proposed element works at the frequency range of 22.8 to 29GHz (23.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), with the relative permittivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}})$</tex> of the LC changes from 2.6 to 3.6.

articleTitle: Design of Elliptical Axicon Phased Metasurface for EM-Wave Diffusion, Enhanced Stealth, and RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach to achieve significant radar cross-section (RCS) reduction in the frequency range of 12 to 22 GHz through the innovative design of an elliptical axicon phased metasurface (EAPM). The integration of geometric phase theory into metasurface design represents a pioneering step toward achieving unprecedented levels of stealth. The objective of this paper is to enhance stealth technology by reducing EM wave reflections and augmenting the stealth capabilities of objects. Through extensive simulations and empirical validation, a remarkable RCS reduction of more than 10 dB across the 12 to 22 GHz frequency range is achieved using the proposed single layer metasurface with elliptical axicon phase distribution. The significant RCS reduction performance is maintained under oblique incidence up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$60^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Design of GBW Extension Technique for Compact Broadband Amplifier Using High-Order Coupled Resonator in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a GBW extension technique using a high-order coupled resonator for broadband amplifiers. A prototype amplifier is realized in a standard 65-nm CMOS technology to achieve fine gain and bandwidth with decent power consumption and a compact chip area. Meanwhile, an output buffer is co-designed with the gain stages to reduce the gain ripple further. With a compact chip area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.088 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, the prototype achieves a differential gain of 20.4 dB and a bandwidth of 21 GHz. The GBW is measured as 220 GHz, which is competitive with the state-of-the-art. The in-band gain and group delay ripples are only 0.9 dB and 14 ps, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Controlled Radiation Pattern Antenna Based on Air-Ground Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a controlled radiation pattern antenna (CRPA) system, which can be utilized in air-ground anti-jamming communication. A simple bent dipole antenna is proposed, capable of achieving effective transmission in vertical direction, with a 3-dB beamwidth of approximately -64° to 64° in the Z-axis direction. Moreover, it also ensures a certain level of transmission capability in the XoY plane. Subsequently, the proposed antenna array is combined with an adaptive anti-jamming algorithm to construct the CRPA system. Through testing, it is demonstrated that this system exhibits higher signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) and practicality compared to CRPA systems utilize traditional antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Current-Carrying Capacity of Chinese YK33 Copper-Based LTCC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology is now widely used in aerospace applications, and it is one of the main technologies to realize the miniaturization of products. In order to solve the problem of high cost and low bending strength of gold-based LTCC, China has developed its own YK33 copper-based LTCC material. Previous studies have demonstrated the material properties and process-ability associated with YK33. In this paper, the current-carrying and heat dissipation capabilities are presented to provide data support for future high-power applications based on YK33.

articleTitle: A Broadband 19.4-34.8GHz LNA MMIC using RLC-Feedback in a 0.15µm GaAs pHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work proposes a three-stage common-source amplification structure broadband millimeter-wave (mm-wave) LNA for fifth-generation (5G) RF front-end transceiver applications. The suggested LNA takes up <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.48 \mathrm{x}0.7mm^{2}$</tex> of chip space and is implemented in a 0.15-µm GaAs pHEMT technology. To get a wideband gain response, a feedback circuit is used in the second and third stages. With a power consumption of 353.4mW from a 2V supply, the LNA achieves a maximum small-signal gain of 20.3 dB and a noise figure (NF) of 1.88-3.85 dB in the 3-dB bandwidth from 19.4 to 34.8GHz. Additionally, the LNA demonstrates an output third-order intercept point ranging from 9.38 to 23.48 dBm and an output 1dB compression point ranging from -2.89 to 5.79 dBm.

articleTitle: Design of a Switchable Microstrip Bandpass Filter with Single- and Dual-Band Functionality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A novel design for a planar microstrip bandpass filter with reconfigurable single and dual-band functionality has been developed. The filter achieves this flexibility by Incorporating switchable grounded ports strategically placed on the input and output coupled lines. Moreover, an auxiliary half-wavelength open stub circuit Integrated into the middle of the coupled lines enhances filter selectivity by providing high attenuation in both the lower and higher stopbands. To demonstrate the concept, a sample switchable bandpass filter was designed. The filter operates at a central frequency of 3.5 GHz in single-band mode, and when switched to dual-band mode, it achieves center frequencies of 2.9 GHz and 4.1 GHz.

articleTitle: A C-Band Current-Steering-Based Variable Gain Low Noise Amplifier with High Temperature Robustness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a C-band variable gain amplifier (VGA). The VGA demonstrates robust performance against gain control under temperature variations. To achieve this, this work modifies the switching signal generation circuit. The measured result indicates that the gain control range of the VGA ranges from 14.49 dB to 15.3 dB with a gain step RMS error of 0.25 dB to 0.57 dB at 5.7 GHz, over the temperature range of −40 °C to 110 °C. In addition, this work analyzes the circuit principle of the current steering with high robustness. This VGA achieves a minimum noise figure of 2.82 dB, an OIP3 of 19.5 dBm, an OP1dB of 8.6 dBm, and a power consumption of 122 mW, all within the range of 4.9 GHz to 6.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of 18-40GHz Micro-Coaxial 0°/180° Hybrid Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents an 18–40 GHz 3-dB 0°/180° hybrid coupler based on 3-D micro-coaxial electrochemical fabrication (MEFAB) process. In the design procedure, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\lambda/4$</tex> branch-line section of the traditional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}/180^{\circ}$</tex> hybrid coupler is replaced by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/4$</tex> diagonal-shorted coupled line section, resulting in a miniaturized size and an enhanced bandwidth performance. In the fabrication process, a 11-layer MEF AB with layer thicknesses of 50 and 100 um is considered to realize the modified hybrid coupler design, which leads to low insertion loss and high fabrication precision. The modified hybrid coupler is first theoretically predicted and then validated by using full-wave simulator CST-MWS. The simulation results show that the hybrid coupler features a 20-dB isolation, 1 dB insertion loss, 0.5 dB amplitude difference, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{\circ}$</tex> phase difference within the entire designed frequency range.

articleTitle: Research on Advanced Technologies of High-Performance CMOS mm-Wave FMCW Synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In recent years, the development of autonomous-driving has put forward strict requirements on millimeter wave radar. As a key module of mm-Wave radar chips, the mm-Wave frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) synthesizer needs to achieve higher performance, such as a larger chirp bandwidth and faster chirp rate. This paper will introduce the architecture of fraction-N phase lock loop (PLL) and the advanced technology for wideband frequency modulation, multi-bank digitally-controlled oscillator (DCO) calibration, and digital predistortion technology for chirp modulation nonlinearity. Finally, the development direction of mm-Wave FMCW frequency synthesizer is prospected.

articleTitle: A Helical Slot Antenna with Grid Reflector for Microwave Directional Ablation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: We present a monopole antenna for microwave ablation of liver tumors. Loading the outer conductor with a grid reflector can change the field distribution so that the antenna produces a directional heating pattern during the ablation process to maximize the protection of healthy tissues around the tumor. By varying the number of helical turns and pitch of the helical slot above the reflector, we can control the area of energy deposition while providing a design solution for miniaturization of the MWA antenna. HFSS and COMSOL were used to simulate the ablation experiment. The findings indicate that at an operating frequency of 2.45GHz and an input power of 20W, continuous ablation for 180s can result in a directional ablation area with a heating depth of 15mm on the active side, and the maximum ablation temperature can reach <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$128^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. Compared with the ordinary reflector, the grid reflector exhibits a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> increase in ablation temperature while maintaining the advantages of lightweight and cost-effectiveness. This provides a promising design option for directional microwave ablation antennas.

articleTitle: A 220-GHz Miniaturized Antenna-Coupled Mixer Based on $\mathbf{Bi}_{2} \mathbf{Sr}_{2} \mathbf{CaCu}_{2} \mathbf{O}_{8}$ Josephson Junction Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a 220-GHz miniaturized slot-antenna-coupled high-temperature superconducting (HTS) mixer, which integrates the HTS junction and the choke filter on one single substrate. The presented mixer utilizes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Bi_{2}}\mathbf{Sr_{2}}\mathbf{CaCu}2\mathbf{O_{8}}$</tex> (BSCCO) intrinsic Josephson junction array as the nonlinear mixing device. To compensate the parasitic capacitance of the BSCCO junction, a short transmission line is used as an inductance for improving impedance matching between the slot antenna and the BSCCO Josephson junction array. The simulation results show that the proposed mixer achieves a conversion gain and noise temperature of -6.74 dB and 266.28 K @ 50K, respectively.

articleTitle: An Efficient Optimization Algorithm for Planar Direct Coupled Filters Based on the End-to-End Surrogate Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In engineering applications, there is a recurrent requirement to adjust the physical parameters of a filter to adapt to variations in indicators such as the center frequency and the operational bandwidth. Traditionally, this process heavily relies on manual expertise and extensive three-dimensional electromagnetic field simulations. Although various experience-independent automatic optimization algorithms have been proposed for filters, they still necessitate the electromagnetic field simulations once the indicators changing, which results in considerable time cost. This paper takes the optimized physical parameters of the planar direct coupled filter as the sample space, and the optimized Latin hypercube sampling method is employed to extract the training samples, which can significantly reduce the number of samples while ensuring the good uniformity and the orthogonality of them. Then the BP Neural Network algorithm is used to obtain an end-to-end surrogate model that directly maps the desired performance indicators to the optimal physical parameters of the filter. The simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm can significantly reduce the time cost of the optimization process while also maintaining preferable prediction accuracy and generalization capability.

articleTitle: A Low-Loss Dual-Band SIW Bandpass Filter (BPF) Based on Through-Silicon-Via (TSV) Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a type of compact low-loss 1/8-mode circular substrate integrated waveguide (CSIW) dual-band bandpass filter (BPF). The resonator of the proposed BPF is fanshaped with the angle of 45°, which obtained by separating the full-mode CSIW. The capacitance-coupling slot between two resonators is determined by its size. Perturbation ThroughSilicon-vias (PTSVs) are introduced to disturb the electrical filed to form the dual-band performance and generated transmission zeros (TZs). The final BPF centered at 17.62 GHz and 33.48 GHz with the fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 45.5% and 22.9%, respectively. The insertion loss (IL) of the dual-band is 0.56 dB and 0.6 dB. The total area of the proposed BPF is 4.14 × 4.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.84 × 0.89 λg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Good agreement is obtained between the simulated and measured results to validate the proposed technique.

articleTitle: A Compact D-Band Power Amplifier with 7.8 dBm Psat in 250 nm InP DHBT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article presents a compact D-band power amplifier (PA) based on 250 nm InP DHBT, which consists of GSG pad and a 4-stage common-emitter. Electromagnetic (EM) simulation results indicate that the S-parameter exhibit favorable input / output return loss (>8dB) covering the whole D-band (110 – 170 GHz), and provides a peak gain of 23.3 dB at 135 GHz, with a 3dB bandwidth spanning 118 to 155 GHz. The PA is designed to produce a saturated output power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>) of 7.8 dBm at 140 GHz, and the P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf> within the frequency range of 120 GHz to 182 GHz is over 7 dBm at the cost power of 70 mW while occupying a compact chip size of only 0.3 × 1.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of the Self-Biased PLL Based Low-Power Low-Jitter Multi-Phase Clock Generator: An Overview (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Multiphase clock generator (MPCG) is an essential building block in high-speed wireless or wireline communication circuits. Compared with other widely used MPCGs, including divider, delay-locked loop and injection-locked oscillators, the self-biased phased-locked loop based MPCG (SBPLL-MPCG) is more attractive to generate a low-jitter clock with lower power. This paper presents an overview of the SBPLL-MCG, including the operation principles, advantages, and two design examples of the MPCG used in a 32-Gb/s PAM4 clock-and-data recovery (CDR) and a 64-Gb/s reference-less PAM4 CDR, respectively.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Extracting a Broadband Small-Signal Model of InP DHBT from 0.2 to 220 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A methodology is proposed for extracting a broadband small-signal model of InP DHBT from 0.2 to 220 GHz, aiming specifically at terahertz (THz) applications. The intrinsic part adopts a π topology, directly extracted from the de-embedded data below 67 GHz. The high frequency data is obtained after on-wafer TRL calibration. Considering the partial interconnection coupling in the device test data after TRL calibration, parasitics of interconnection coupling are taken into account in the model topology. The corresponding extraction method is provided for each parameter. Based on the proposed model topology and extraction method, a comparison between test values and simulated values demonstrates good agreement within the range of 0.2-220 GHz.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Wideband Transimpedance Amplifier with Adaptive Phase Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Micro Electro Mechanical Systems (MEMS) oscillators are increasingly utilized in wireless communication for their merits of high frequency, compact size, and low cost. Especially, capacitive MEMS oscillators are noted for the higher frequency and superior quality factor. To form a high-performance MEMS oscillator, this paper presents a novel transimpedance amplifier (TIA) with an adaptive phase compensation scheme to actuate a t50MHz 343kΩ capacitive MEMS resonator. The proposed TIA employs a tunable phase-shifter controlled by a PLL-based adaptive loop to meet the oscillation requirement. Based on the TSMC 40nm CMOS process, the proposed TIA was elaborately designed. The simulated 2ain is 6t.4dBΩ and the input-referred current noise is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24\text{pA}/\sqrt{}\text{Hz}$</tex>. Thanks to the novel adaptive loop, the simulated phase of the output voltage is nearly in-phase with the input current. The power consumption is 8.9mW under 1.1V/ 3.3V dual supplies.

articleTitle: Effect of Ground Solder Ball Failure on Signal Interference between Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: As a high-density package, ball grid arrays (BGA) are widely used in electronic products. However, the complex environment may lead to solder ball failure, which in turn causes serious inter-channel crosstalk. For this problem, this paper researched the effect of ground solder ball failure on inter-channel crosstalk in terms of high-frequency parameters and time-domain waveforms. Firstly, an electromagnetic field model of two signal transmission channels with BGA packages was developed to analyze effect of the solder ball failure on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> parameters. Then, a time-domain simulation system of the two signal transmission channels was also developed to analyze effect of the solder ball failure on the time domain signal waveforms. Finally, frequency-domain and time-domain tests were conducted to verify these simulation models and conclusions.

articleTitle: A $Ka$-Band Low-Phase-Noise Phase-locked Loop with Reconfigurable Output Network for Fundamental and Push-Push Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance Ka-band phase-locked loop (PLL) with a reconfigurable output network, fabricated using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS technology. The oscillator core employs a series gain-stage topology and class-E load network to significantly boost output power. The reconfigurable output network incorporates two reflection-type phase shifters, which not only provide phase shifting capabilities but also serve as a mode selector, allowing the PLL to switch between fundamental and second harmonic outputs. This design achieves impressive performance metrics, featuring a minimum phase noise of -105 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset with an output power of 6 dBm in the frequency range of 24.2-24.6 GHz. When operating in push-push mode, the PLL delivers second-harmonic output powers exceeding -12 dBm across the entire frequency range. Compared to other reported CMOS works, this design demonstrates comparable performance and is suitable for advanced clock generations.

articleTitle: A Capacitor-Less LDO with Fast Response and Transient Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A capacitor-less low-dropout (LDO) regulator with fast response and transient enhancement is proposed in this paper. Based on the 130-nm CMOS process, an off-chip capacitor-less LDO with the advanced Q-reduction to enhance the transient response is designed with an input voltage of 1.5 V, an output voltage of 1.24 V. When the load current changes from 0.1 mA to 200 mA, the rise and fall time are 50 ns, and the response time is 278 mV and 124 mV respectively for the undershoot voltage and overshoot voltage within 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathbf{s}$</tex>, which can provide a stable power supply to the load that jumps rapidly.

articleTitle: Terahertz Planar Dual-Polarization Quadrature Mixer for Fiber-THz-Fiber High-Speed Wireless Link (invited paper)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Polarization multiplexing technology has the advantages of double data rate and bidirectional communication, which is an effective way to improve the channel capacity and spectrum utilization of communication systems in the future. However, the existing THz polarization multiplexing front-end circuits are faced with the key problems such as poor isolation, unbalance of amplitude and phase and difficult planar integration. In this paper, a novel and compact architecture of planar integrated dual-polarization quadrature mixer is proposed, focusing on the design of THz amplitude-phase balanced quadrature mixers. Based on anti-parallel Schottky diodes, a quadrature subharmonic mixer in the 330 GHz band has been designed. Measurement results show that, the single sideband conversion loss is 10.5-13.5 dB in the range of 310-348 GHz, and the image rejection ratio is basically better than 15 dB. The THz quadrature mixer proposed in this paper can be used as an optical fiber extender or THz wireless bridge to establish high-speed wireless links in areas where optical fibers are difficult or expensive to lay out.

articleTitle: A Low-Loss 92–96 GHz Power Combiner Using Silicon-Integrated Suspended Line (Si-ISL)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article presents a novel silicon-integrated suspended line (Si-ISL) power combiner circuit implemented in the microe-lectromechanical system (MEMS) process. In this design, the self-packaging characteristics of the integrated suspended line (ISL) platform are fully utilized to minimize radiation losses. At the same time, the signal trace of the Si-ISL is formed by using gold-surrounded silicon to minimize the dielectric loss caused by the silicon wafer. From 92 GHz to 96 GHz, the back-to-back power combiner for the Si-ISL exhibits an insertion loss of just 0.5 dB, with a return loss exceeding 25 dB. For the transition structure from rectangular waveguide (RWG) to Si-ISL, the back-to-back insertion loss remains below 0.26 dB, and the return loss exceeds 28 dB.

articleTitle: Enhanced Breakdown Voltage of p-GaN HEMT with a Lateral Gradient in Barrier Layer Component
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, an optimized enhanced-mode p-GaN high electron mobility transistor (p-GaN HEMT) is proposed, in which the barrier layer is set into a composite structure with a lateral gradient of Aluminum component (LGC) from the drain edge under the gate towards both source and drain, respectively. By leveraging the polarization effects from different heterojunctions, a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) with gradually changing density is formed laterally in the channel layer, which more precisely modulates the electric field distribution in the gate-drain region, enhances the voltage resistance of it, and reduces leakage current, thereby enhancing the breakdown voltage of the device and improving the output performance. The breakdown voltage of the proposed optimized LGC-HEMT under simulation is 716.73V, which is 13.1 % higher than that of the conventional p-GaN HEMT (633.64V), while the specific on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n},\mathrm{s}\mathrm{p}})$</tex> is only 1.34 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m\Omega\cdot cm^{2}$</tex>, and the Baliga's figure of merit (BFOM) changes from 216.42 to 382.68 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$MW/cm^2$</tex>, which is 76.82% higher, hinting at the promising potential of the proposed HEMT.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability Assurance of Microvia Metallization on High Purity Alumina Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a set of innovative measures including design processability, microvia forming technology, seed layer deposition and microvia plating technology are proposed to ensure the reliability of the microvia metallisation on high-purity alumina substrate. Improved quality of the microvia metallisation withstood the reliability test. The reliability assurance technology of microvia metallisation on high purity alumina substrate is confirmed.

Author Keywords: high purity alumina substrate; microvia metallization; reliability assurance technology

articleTitle: The Design of Broadband Ultra-Wide-Angle Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A new kind of broadband ultra-wide-angle absorber is designed in this paper. The resistors resonators in the top layer acts as electric dipoles. The resistance film in the middle responses as magnetic dipoles. The simulation results show that for the TE polarized wave, the absorption band is 8. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\sim 15\text{GHz}$</tex> with the incidence angle can in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}\sim 70^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Voltage Controlled Oscillator Based Sensing for Frequency Synthesizer with Capacitor Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article presents frequency synthesizer with capacitor switching with analog to digital converter (ADC) for voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) based sensor. The proposed frequency synthesizer applied to the 5GHz CMOS for frequency compensation, which includes a phase frequency comparator (PFD), a current charge pump, and a channel selection frequency divider (pulse-swallow counter) and pre-scaler.

articleTitle: Research on One-Dimensional Photonic Crystal Trace Analyte Detection and Sensing Based on 1.37THz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: At present, terahertz (THz) absorption spectroscopy technology has shown vast application prospects in the field of fingerprint sensing. However, the detection of trace analytes using traditional methods is still very challenging. This paper proposes a terahertz absorption spectrum enhancement method based on a one-dimensional photonic crystal defect structure, which can greatly enhance the interaction between terahertz waves and trace substances. Based on the Fabry-Perot resonance effect, the local field around the analyte can be enhanced by changing the length of the photonic crystal defect cavity. When lactose film is used as the analyte, a series of resonant peaks can be obtained by changing the length of the defect cavity in one-dimensional photonic crystals. The enhanced broadband fingerprint spectrum is obtained. By connecting the envelope lines of a series of resonant peaks. When finally detecting 0.2um of α-lactose, approximately 71 times the absorption enhancement factor can be achieved. The detection frequency range has been increased from the traditional 0.529 THz to 1.37 THz, fully utilizing terahertz spectrum resources and providing a new method for enhancing the detection of terahertz absorption spectra of trace analytes.

articleTitle: Study on the Preparation Process of Metal Thin-Film based on Barium Titanate-Based Ceramic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Barium titanate ceramics are important ferroelectric materials, which can be used in multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs), phase shifters, ferroelectric memories and so on. Due to the loose structure and rough surface, metallization thin-film on barium titanate ceramics suffer from a more obvious problem of poor adhesion. Increasing the thickness of the underlying metal and using two technical routes of atomic layer deposition (ALD), by comparing the surface state of the metal film and the film adhesion before and after the improvement, it is proved that either by thickening the thickness of the adhesion layer or by changing the chemical components of the interface of the metal film layer, the adhesion of the metal film can be improved, and the thin-film circuits based on barium titanate ceramics can satisfy the requirements of the use.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Variable Gain Amplifier with a Gain Adjustment Range of 16-dB in 65-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A Ka-band variable gain amplifier (VGA) with large amplitude adjustment range and low phase variation is presented in this paper, which is fabricated in commercial 65-nm CMOS process. The VGA core cicuit is composed of 6-bit proportional gain-cell, which contains two complementary numerical-control differential amplifiers. The results show that the frequency of this single-stage VGA covers form 31.5GHz to 40GHz within 3dB drop in Gain. Besides the 6-bit VGA achieves a gain adjustment range of 16-dB within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5^{\circ}$</tex> of phase variations. The chip core area is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$330\times 200\ \text{um}^{2}$</tex> •

articleTitle: Integrated Wireless Real-Time Glucose Sensing System Using Copper-Nickel Composite SPE Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a flexible non-enzymatic sweat glucose sensor loaded with copper-nickel composite nanomaterials on carbon electrode integrated with wireless monitoring system were developed. The non-enzymatic glucose sensor was fabricated efficiently and simply by electrodepositing copper-nickel bimetallic composite on a carbon-based screen-printing electrode (Cu-Ni/CSPE). Besides, a wireless monitoring system for glucose detection was designed and composed with a signal processing circuit using ADUCM355 chip. The results of electrocatalytic experiments showed that the sensitivity of the Cu-Ni/C-SPE sensor was 5507.4 μA/(mM∙cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), the linear detection range was 25 μM∼2.275 mM, the detection limit was 0.149 μM, and the response time was < 1s.

articleTitle: Overview of Wide-Stopband Substrate-Integrated Waveguide Bandpass Filters and Multiplexers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The overview of wide-stopband substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) bandpass filters (BPFs) and multiplexers are presented, the realization schemes with respect to the merits and drawbacks are summarized and classified into following types, i.e., introducing lowpass filters (LPFs), producing transmission zeros (TZs), staggering higher-order mode resonances, controlling couplings, and pushing higher-order mode resonances. Current research status is summarized and the future development vision is also proposed, including the promising outlooks and study obstacles pertaining the progress of wide-stopband SIW filtering devices.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Channel High-Isolation Up-Conversion Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband, high rejection and high isolation dual-channel up-conversion module is designed and implemented by means of double up-conversion. The ultra-high isolation of the module improves the receiving dynamic of the analog simulation systems by more than 15 dB. The article provides the schematic diagram of the module and the specific circuit design of each branch, and analyzes the key indicators of the module. The test results show that the inter channel isolation degree of the module is ≥ 90dBc, the intra band amplitude flatness is ≤ ± 1.5dB, and the harmonic suppression is ≥ 30dBc, meeting the design specifications.

articleTitle: A Ku-band TRX Front-End With High Performance In 0.15-μm GaAs PHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A time-division duplex (TDD) transmit/receive (T/R) Ku-band (15 GHz ~ 18 GHz) front-end in 0.15-μm GaAs for phased array radars is presented. The front-end consists of a power amplifier (PA), a low noise amplifier (LNA), and a single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch. In this work, a transistor stacked switch is proposed with high-power-handling capability (simulated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{IP}_{1\text{dB}} > 34.7\text{dB})$</tex> and low insertion loss (IL) over the band. A power combining and dividing matching network is designed for outputting large power. A three-stage current-reuse LNA is introduced to reduce the power consumption. Measurements show that, in transmitting mode, the PA achieves the maximum output power of 28.6 ~ 29.3 dBm and the peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 35.7 ~ 44.5 % over the band. In receiving mode, the LNA achieves a gain of 19.9 ~20.9 dB and a noise figure (NF) of 2.8 ~4 dB while drawing 34.4 mA from 3.3 V supply. The overall chip area is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, including pads.

articleTitle: A Chipless RFID Sensor for Ethanol Solution Concentration Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The research of chipless radio frequency identification (RFID) sensor is rapidly becoming a very interesting field in the application space of the modern Internet of Things. In this paper, a chipless RFID sensor based on split-ring resonator is proposed for the concentration detection of ethanol solution. The radar cross section (RCS) is simulated in the design stage, and the equivalent circuit under the excitation of incident wave is given. The sensor does not require antenna and feeder integration, and realizes wireless passive detection of ethanol solution. By analyzing the amplitude - frequency response and phase response of 20% - 100% ethanol solutions, the fitting curves of amplitude and resonance frequency were obtained respectively, which proved its strong correlation with ethanol concentration. The sensitivity based on amplitude and resonant frequency is 0.002 dB/% and 0.37 MHz/% respectively, which can be used for quantitative detection of ethanol solution. The ideal characteristics of such a sensor include low cost, environmental friendliness, easy integration, and flexible application in various fields. It provides a new idea for the application of RF biosensors.

articleTitle: A Broadband Circularly-Polarized Transmitarray Based on Independent Control of Dual Linear Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A broadband circularly polarized (CP) magneto-electric dipole transmitarray with low cross-polarization level is proposed in this paper. The proposed transmitarray element integrates L probe feeding structures and differential feeding structures in two orthogonal directions, respectively, thereby enabling independent control of the transmission waves for dual linear polarizations. Based on this characteristic, a CP element employing the element rotation method is designed. Moreover, the continuous phase-tuning schematic is adopted to realize a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16\times 16{-}$</tex> element CP transmitarray. And the simulated results demonstrate a broad 1-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 43.5% and a 1-dB gain bandwidth of 30.4%. The proposed design is highly suitable for applications requiring high-purity CP waves.

articleTitle: A Performance Study of Layout in 0.13um CMOS Power Amplifier for 4G Mobile Front-End Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work presents the performance improvements of optimized layout in 0.13um CMOS Power Amplifier (PA) for 4G multimode multiband transmitter frond-end module (TXM). The TXM including the 0.13um CMOS PA, SP16T antenna switch and all passive components is fully integrated in a flip-chip LGA package. In order to show the improvements of novel layout geometry, the performances of the whole TXM have been compared directly. Compared with conventional layout structure, the measurement results of this work improve maximum linear output power and power-added efficiency (PAE) by 0.5dB and 3.5% in 915MHz EDGE mode. It also pushes the linear power to 27.5dBm in 1800MHz EDGE mode and 24.3dBm in TD-LTE mode. The novel layout geometry also shows better the thermal performance and reliability at high temperature.

articleTitle: A 220-GHz Wireless Communication System Using a Quasi-Optical Cryogenic Receiver of High Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a 220-GHz wireless communication system by using a quasi-optical cryogenic receiver of high sensitivity. The presented terahertz (THz) communication system utilizes a quasi-optical cryogenic receiver with a noise factor much lower than that of conventional room-temperature counterpart, thus helping to increase the transmission distance in long-range communication scenarios. In the scaled wireless link experiment, the communication data rate achieves 10 Gbit/s for a 16-quadrature amplitude modulation. According to the link budget, the communication distance can be around 5 km provided using appropriate transmitter power and antenna gains for practical scenarios. Considering the small volume, light weight and high sensitivity of the cryogenic receiver, the proposed system should be very useful for long-range THz communication applications.

articleTitle: 28-GHz Low-Loss and High-Selectivity WIPD Filtering Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-miniaturized and WIPD-based power divider with low loss and high selectivity. To reduce footprint and loss, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> phase shift for the power division was realized by a lumped-element <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> model, where one of the shunt capacitors is absorbed in the nearby capacitor of the filter's parallel resonator. To improve the roll-off rate, a cascade of the parallel-series resonators was used to generate two transmission zeros (TZs) beside the passband. A two-pole filtering power divider was prototyped. At 26.5 GHz, the measured minimum insertion loss, return loss, and output isolation are 1.6 dB, 17.5 dB, and 28 dB, respectively. Three transmission zeros at 18 GHz, 32.65 GHz, and 37.64 GHz are obtained. The measured 30-dB rectangle coefficient is 2. The core size is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.408 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A 1.7-2.7 GHz High Linear Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In order to meet the high linearity and low noise requirements in the receiving channels of 5.5G, this paper proposes a low noise amplifier (LNA) with a shutdown function (PD) based on the 0.25 μm GaAs pHEMT. Utilizing a cascade structure, the amplifier incorporates a RC feedback network, along with active bias network for the common-source and common-gate to enhance linearity. Through input and output matching, minimum noise and maximum power output are achieved. Experimental results demonstrate that the chip operates at the frequency range of 1.7-2.7 GHz with a gain of 18–22 dB. The input and output return loss are less than -10 dB, with a 1dB output compression point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{P}_{1\text{dB}})$</tex> of 22.5 dBm. The noise figure is less than 1 dB with an input third-order intercept point (IIP3) of 23 dBm. The switching time of the shut-down and the turn-on is less than 20 ns and 50 ns, respectively.

articleTitle: Characterization and Study on MOSFET Source/Drain Series Resistance Down to 4 K
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: MOSFET Source/Drain parasitic series resistance, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{SD}$</tex>, is an important parameter for short channel device. But characterization and study at cryogenic temperature is relatively scarce. This paper presents a systematic study of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{SD}$</tex> extracted from the mobility constant method down to 4 K for the first time. In addition, the anomalous behavior of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{SD}$</tex> with temperature lowering from 300 K to 4 K is interpreted by combined effects of dopant freezeout and mobility increase due to less phonon scattering. Furthermore, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{SD}$</tex> change with width scaling combined with temperature effects on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{SD}$</tex> is also discussed.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of AMC-Based Antenna for UHF RFID Metal-Resistant Tags
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a UHF RFID metal-resistant tag antenna is designed by using the loaded AMC substrate method to achieve the metal-resistant performance, and the bent dipole antenna as the radiator. The antenna structure parameters are optimized using the Improved Beetle Swarm Optimization (IBSO) Algorithm, with an overall size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$82.9\times 45.1\times 3.8\text{mm}^{3}$</tex>, which meets at 860~960 MHz, and the maximum reading distance averages up to 14 m under the UHF RFID standard in China. The structure has low fabricate cost, no complex structure such as over-hole, and can be completely processed by PCB process.

articleTitle: Miniature Dual-Band Quadrature Coupler for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A miniaturized dual-band quadrature coupler design suitable for millimeter-wave applications is presented in this paper. To largely reduce the circuit size of the proposed coupler while achieving the desired dual-band frequency characteristics, the dual-band design of bridged T-coil is employed. Specifically, a proposed 18.7/38.5-GHz dual-band quadrature coupler is realized in IPD with a compact circuit size of 1.4 mm x 1.4 mm. Good measured performance is observed., and the feasibility of the dual-band design of bridged T-coil for millimeter-wave applications is thus validated.

articleTitle: Parametric Modeling of The Series-fed Patch Antenna Design Based on Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this work, we propose a parametric model based on deep neural networks for series-fed patch antenna design for millimeter-wave automotive radar. In this proposed model, the modified football team training algorithm (MFTTA) is used to improve the accuracy of deep learning network (DNN). Then, based on the improved deep learning network, a parametric model of the antenna is established, taking the antenna's result parameters as input and the reflection coefficient as the output of the antenna. To verify the accuracy of the proposed MFTTA - DNN model, we establish a parametric model of a series-fed antenna operating at a frequency of 77 GHz. The results show that the MSE error of MFTTA-DNN is 0.268, which is less than that of DNN, indicating that the performance of the proposed MFTTA-DNN model is good.

articleTitle: Ultrathin Conformal Transmitarray via Huygens' Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency conformal transmitarray is accomplished via ultrathin dual-layer Huygens' metasurface. The Huygens' unit cell consists a pair of antisymmetric metallic structures printed on a thin dielectric substrate, only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1\lambda$</tex>. By tuning the magnetic and electric resonances simultaneously, the transmitting phase can be manipulated in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$360^{\circ}$</tex> range. When the proposed Huygens' unit cells are arranged on a cylindrical surface to form a conformal transmitarray, the simulated gain can achieve 26.54 dBi, namely the aperture efficiency of 55.4%.

articleTitle: A 1.52-dB-Insertion-Loss, V-Band Coupled Bandpass Filter with a Three-Dimensional Metal Coaxial Structure Using 3D Printing and MEMS Hybrid Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a coupled bandpass filter with a three-dimensional metal coaxial structure using 3D printing and MEMS hybrid technology. It achieves low-loss at high frequency while ensuring ease of processing and low cost. The HFSS software simulation results verify that the process using 3D printing has the same filtering performance as the traditional MEMS process. The design, with the filter size of 11.52 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 0.6$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 0.5$</tex> mm, operates in the V-band and achieves a return loss of greater than 15 dB and an insertion loss of 1.52 dB within the frequency range of 57~67 GHz.

articleTitle: A 24 GHz VCO in a 180 nm SiGe BiCMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article presents a 24 GHz voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) in a 180 nm SiGe BiCMOS process with 1.8 V voltage supply. The design incorporates an optimized LC tank circuit and a capacitive divider in the feedback path of the cross-coupled differential pair. Measurement results indicate a phase noise of −106.2 dBc/Hz and a figure of merit (FoM) of −180 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset, a tuning range spanning from 23 GHz to 25 GHz and an ouput power of 3 dBm. The VCO occupies a die area of only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.26 \ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex> including the output matching.

articleTitle: Federated Learning-Empowered Resource Allocation Optimisation for E-Health IoT System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel federated learning (FL)-enabled resource allocation optimization framework for e-health IoT systems. The framework leverages a three-level transmission architecture, including local training, wireless transmission, and global training levels. We model the delay and energy consumption for each level and formulate a joint optimization problem to minimize the long-term average system cost by jointly optimizing UE selection, transmission power, and computation resource allocation. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in reducing delay and energy consumption while maintaining privacy in e-health IoT systems.

articleTitle: The Design and Analysis for Improving the Power-Efficiency of Ring-VCO Based PLL (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The ring-VCO-based clock generator has gained much interest due to its compact area but suffers from poor performance. To enhance power efficiency while maintaining performance, this paper presents several promising techniques and provides a detailed analysis, including a discussion of the jitter impact on analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). This examination aims to facilitate a more comprehensive evaluation of phase locked loops (PLLs) performance straightforwardly and accurately.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Neural Network Model for Accelerating Quantum Transport Simulation of FinFET by Non-Equilibrium Green's Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The simulation of quantum transport in semiconductor devices is time-consuming, and methods to reduce computation cost are required. In this paper, we propose a method to accelerate the quantum transport simulation of FinFET by using convolutional neural network (CNN) to get a relatively accurate initial guess of potential distribution, which can effectively reduce the number of iteration loops. Geometrical parameters, doping concentration and applied voltage are set as the input of CNN model, the potential distribution in cross section of FinFET with different geometrical parameters, doping concentrations and applied voltage can be obtained. Compared with the traditional method which sets the initial potential distribution to be a specific value according to applied voltage, our proposed method can reduce the simulation time by 45%.

articleTitle: An 8×8 Phased-Array Antenna System with Wide Axial-Ratio Bandwidth and Beam-Width for SATCOM Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article presents a wideband scalable 17.7-21.2 GHz 64-element SATCOM phased-array receiver. The phased array uses a full RF beamforming architecture with 64 dual circular polarization (CP) antenna elements and 16 16-channel silicon beamformers (BFs) based on a printed circuit board (PCB). The microstrip stacked patch antenna is series-fed using an arc-shaped feed network followed by two cross-shaped coupling slots to generate dual CP waves. The top radiating patch uses a double-layer metasurface to extend antenna impedance bandwidth. Simulation and measurement results verify the performance of the proposed receiver, demonstrating dual beams, wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and beam-width, excellent polarization purity, low sidelobes, and wide-angle scanning capability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\pm 60^{\circ})$</tex>.

Author Keywords: wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and beam-width

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband RF Transceiver Microsystem Based on Wafer Lever 3D Silicon Package
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: To miniaturized and lightweight RF transceiver front-ends for communication, telemetry, detection and other multi-scenarios over a wide frequency range, this paper designs a transceiver microsystem with an operating frequency covering the C. Ku band. Based on the silicon-based 3D heterogeneous integration process, the low-noise amplifier, power amplifier, multifunctional reconfigurable transmitter chip, multifunctional reconfigurable receiver chip and other chips are integrated in high density to form an ultra-wideband RF transceiver microsystem. The microsystem has a transmission power of more than 100 mW, a receive noise figure of 3.88 dB and a reception gain of more than 70 dB in the 4–18 GHz operating band. The size of the RF transceiver microsystem is 17 mm× 10 mm×l.8 mm, which realizes miniaturization, generalization and reconfigurable integration.

articleTitle: 1000W Shortwave Power Amplifier Temperature Dependent Characteristics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Aimed to research the characteristic of shortwave power amplifier with temperature, the temperature experiments are performed at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-25\ {}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}, 0\ {}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}, 25\ {}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$55\ {}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. The results showed that with the temperature increasing from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-25\ {}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$55\ {}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, there is a significant downward trend for its performance. In detail, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{ds}}$</tex>, Pout, gain, PAE and IM decrease 1.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}, 1.2\ \text{dB}$</tex>, 1.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}, 0.69$</tex> % and 3 dB in 16 MHz, respectively. These results indicate that the performance of this 1000 W shortwave PA is significantly affected with temperature variation. Therefore, the corresponding remedy measure is designed to counteract the index degradation of this 1000 W shortwave P A. This can provide important guidance for the reliability design of 1000 W shortwave power amplifier.

articleTitle: 340 GHz Single-Layer Antenna on Chip (AoC) Using Higher Order Mode Resonance Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Antenna on Chip (AoC) provides a promising solution to reduce the interconnection loss between on-chip system circuits and off-chip antennas in terahertz (THz) bands. In this paper, a 2 ×2 slot array on chip along with its modified version of L-shape slots are presented and designed. Two parallel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TH}_{20}$</tex> 1 resonant cavities are employed to feed the slot array and both higher order resonant modes are excited by a grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW). The proposed antenna features a simple array feeding network and high gain, making it a viable option for THz communication and radar applications.

articleTitle: Monolithic Transimpedance Amplifier Design for 343K-ohm 150MHz Capacitive MEMS Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Capacitive MEMS disk resonators with high frequency and high quality factor can be used as frequency references in 6G/THz wireless transceivers. However, they exhibit ultrahigh motional resistance. This paper presents a 125-dBΩ 955-MHz 11-mW CMOS transimpedance amplifier (TIA) to drive them with low power consumption. This TIA employs two identical inverted-based Cherry-Hooper amplifiers with stable bias and phase compensation to obtain high gain and nearly zero closed-loop phase shift. The proposed TIA successfully actuates the 343-KΩ 150-MHz MEMS resonator, and oscillation builds up within 180 µs with a swing of 1.3 Vp-p. The simulated phase noise of the MEMS oscillator is -71 dBc/Hz at 1 kHz offset and -98 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset. Implemented on a 0.18 µm CMOS process, the TIA consumes just 11 mW under two 1.8 V/ 1.6 V supplies.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra-Wide Stopband DMS Microstrip Low-Pass Filter and Optimization With Tab-Transformer Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: It is difficult to balance the requirements of wide stopband, low loss and miniaturization in microstrip low-pass filter design. To solve the problem, a combination of loading the defected metal structure (DMS) units and Tab-Transformer neural network is adopted in this paper. Firstly, the T-shaped DMS unit is introduced into the microstrip metal surface of the high and low impedance line microstrip filter, and the structure optimization of the DMS unit is carried out by using the Tab- Transformer neural network algorithm, which significantly improves the passband performance and reduces the size of the filter. Then the defected ground structure (DGS) unit is loaded on the ground plane of the filter. By fine-tuning the size of the DGS and the microstrip parallel branch, the harmonic of the filter stopband is further suppressed and the pass-band loss of the filter is also reduced. The test results show that the optimized design of the filter has a passband cutoff frequency of 2 GHz, a passband insertion loss of ≤ 0.1 dB, a return loss S11 reduced to -15.49 dB, and a stopband rejection S21 below -20 dB in the frequency range of 2.73 GHz-15.39 GHz, whereas the area of 20 mm* 18.75 mm meets the anti-harmonic interference of a certain L-band radar, low loss and miniaturization requirements.

articleTitle: Research on Large-Scale Fading Characteristics of Radio Propagation in High-Speed Maglev Millimeter Wave Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, the radio propagation characteristics are studied in the high-speed maglev millimeter wave communication system. Based on the ray tracing technology, studies the influence of antenna polarization mode, antenna beam width and base station operating frequency on the large-scale fading characteristics of millimeter wave in the typical operation scenarios of high-speed maglev, which providing a reference for the design and optimization of high-speed maglev millimeter wave communication system.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality-Assisted EEG Biomarker to Identify the Neural Differentiation of Dementia by Graph Theory Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: As a chronic progressive and neurodegenerative disorder to threaten elders worldwide, dementia always gradually develops from mild forgetfulness to severe cognitive decline and covers several clinical conditions including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Mild cognition impairment (MCI). Timely and precise diagnosis of patients with different dementia diseases are essential for effectively medical intervention. Virtual reality (VR) has been proved to activate functional connectivity among multiple cortical regions to varying degrees for humans with different cognitive levels, presenting good potential to take part in neuropsychological test especially for dementia. Electroencephalography (EEG) is commonly used to clinically evaluate the brain activity of neurological diseases such as epilepsy, sleep disorders, and brain tumors, with good time resolution. Graph theory can robustly represent the topological properties of intricate brain functional connectivity based on EEG data. Accordingly, we convene AD patients, MCI patients, and healthy controls, to watch VR 3D videos and simultaneously measure their EEG data to constitute the functional networks. The p-values statistically demonstrated a neural differentiation of the functional small-world network among AD, MCI, and normal controls under 3D cognitive loads. The significantly different functional connectivities between three dementia groups indicate that the 3D simulation expertise can be applied in clinical dementia diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Frequency Doubler with 40 dBc Fundamental Suppression in 0.1-μm GaAs pHEMT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency doubler with an output amplifier based on 0.1 µm GaAs pHEMT technology. The frequency doubler consists of balanced diodes, a power combining balun and a two-stage output amplifier. The amplitude and phase imbalances of the employed balun are both less than 0.33° within the operating frequency range. The simulated results of the optimized circuit demonstrate that the frequency doubler achieves a conversion gain greater than 3.6 dB and an output power higher than 17.6 dBm from 20 GHz to 30 GHz. The fundamental suppression at 25 GHz is over 60 dBc, and the third harmonic suppression in the entire frequency band is greater than 30 dBc.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of Electrothermal Coupling on TSV Transmission Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the transmission characteristics of double-layer tapered through-silicon vias (TSVs) within the frequency range of 0.1 to 100 GHz using COMSOL. We introduce the temperature-dependent electrothermal properties of various materials. The influence of electrothermal coupling on the signal transmission coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{21}$</tex> is quantified. Several parameters affecting electrothermal coupling are analyzed. The results show that the electrothermal coupling will reduce the signal transmission coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{21}$</tex> by 0.003 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 0.01dB in the frequency range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0. 1\sim$</tex> 1 GHz and increase by 0. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$07\sim 0.27\text{dB}$</tex> in the frequency range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\sim 100\text{GHz}$</tex>. Increasing the external heat source, signal magnitude, TSV height, or RDL length will enhance the electrothermal coupling effect, leading to greater changes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{21}$</tex> compared to room temperature.

articleTitle: Coupling Reduction in 2D Antenna Array With Ultra-Small Spacing Using Phase-Shift Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a phase-shift metasurfacebased decoupling method for closely spaced two-dimensional (2D) antenna array. Under oblique incidence, the smoother phase curves and frequency shifts of the metasurface contribute to a wider decoupling bandwidth. The phase shift metasurface is applied to a 1 × 2 E-plane and H-plane patch antenna pair, achieving decoupling in both port isolation and radiation pattern. Furthermore, the proposed decoupling method is extended to a 2 × 2 planar array with a small center-to-center spacing of 0.32Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and an edge-to-edge spacing of 0.038Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free space wavelength at the center frequency). Notably, the isolations improve from 7 dB to 21 dB for H-plane coupling, from 11 dB to 13 dB for Eplane coupling, and from 10 dB to 19 dB for D-plane coupling.

articleTitle: Deep Kernel Polynomial Chaos Expansion Technique for Uncertainty Quantification of Electronic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) of electronic circuits using Monte Carlo (MC) simulations is highly time-consuming. Performing UQ based on surrogate models of electronic circuits is more efficient. In this paper, a surrogate modeling technique based on a deep kernel polynomial chaos expansion (DKPCE) is applied to UQ of an electronic link with 119 uncertain parameters. DKPCE combines the deep neural network (DNN) and polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). It can efficiently predict circuit responses by taking uncertain parameters of electronic circuits as inputs. Moreover, the statistical moments of circuit responses such as the mean and variance can be analytically computed through the model parameters of DKPCE. A numerical example of an electronic link is provided for validation. It is shown that DKPCE achieves higher accuracy compared to the DNN models and PCE models in the UQ of electronic circuits. Moreover, it realizes a speedup of 8. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times$</tex> compared to circuit MC simulations.

articleTitle: Research Progress of Transformer-Based mm-Wave Fundamental Oscillators in CMOS (invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: At mm-wave frequency, an oscillator's phase noise performance is crucial to high-speed communication systems and high-resolution radar systems. In CMOS technology, a mm-wave oscillator with low phase noise and high output power is chal-lenging due to its limited metal quality factor and supply voltage. In this paper, two oscillator designs with fundamental oscillator performance enhancement are summarized. In both designs, on-chip transformers are applied with a Class-F operation, a boosted negative conductance, and an improved quality factor. The phase noise performance can be improved. The measured results show the 66.4 GHz DCO achieves a phase noise of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-98.2$</tex> dBc/Hz at <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>MHz offset while the 51.5 GHz VCO achieves a phase noise of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-96.12$</tex> dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset.

articleTitle: An E-Band 360°4-bits Switched-Type Phase Shifter in 65-nm CMOS Process for 300-GHz Phased Array Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: An E-band <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$360^{\circ}4$</tex> -bit switched-type phase shifter (PS) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$28^{\circ}$</tex> phase adjustment in 65-nm CMOS process is presented in this paper. The proposed phase shifter is based on the switched-type and the reflection-type topology. The PS combines four series phase shift bits to achieve a relative phase shift ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$337.5^{\circ}$</tex> with a step of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$22.5^{\circ}$</tex>. The PS is designed using two switched-type phase shifting topologies: the inductor-based T-type and a high-flow-pass network. To reduce phase error at each state, a reflection-type structure is used to alter the phase. From the measurement results, the proposed E-band phase shifter achieves a RMS phase error of 1.9-3 degrees and a RMS gain error of 1.49-2.5 dB from 63- to 81-GHz. The output return loss and the input return loss are better than −14 and −7 dB. The total area of this circuit with pads is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.49 \ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, and the core area of the proposed phase shifter is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.28 \ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Ka-Band AFSIW Power Divider and Coupler for Millimeter-wave Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents Ka-band power divider and coupler based on the air-filled substrate integrated waveguide (AFSIW) technology. The utilization of air as the dielectric material in SIW structures offers reduced dielectric losses and enhanced performance for high-frequency applications. The AFSIW devices demonstrate lower loss, higher quality factor, and increased power handling capabilities compared to conventional SIW designs. These compact and lightweight components provide improved efficiency and isolation for millimeter-wave wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A 2-18G Multi-Stage Distributed Amplifier Using Chebyshev Matching Network for Efficiency Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article presents a quadruple-stackced CMOS distributed power amplifier (DPA)implemented in 65nm CMOS process. To enhance the output power and power added efficiency, A Chebyshev artificial transmission line is used as output matching network, while a one-stage DPA works as a preamplifier for wideband matching and gain enhancement. The DPA provides 20.5-dB gain and 35-GHz 3-dB BW from 2 to 37GHz with gain variation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm0.65\text{ dE }$</tex> from 2-34G. The DPA realizes 17.4-20.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{P}_{sat}, 13.7-16.6 \text{OP}_{1dB}$</tex> from 2-18G with the maximum 24.9% PAE at 2 GHz.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Planar Antenna with Radiating Element Notch and Ground Notch Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: An different planar band-notched characteristics antennas is presented in this paper. Consisting of a radiation patch that has an improved 山-shape slot, M-shape slot, and two mirror images of each other C-shape slots embedded in reference ground. it will have band-notched characteristics in the WiMAX band, which range from 3.3 to 3.6 GHz, lower WLAN (which frequency is close to 5.2 GHz), higher WLAN (which frequency is close to 5.8 GHz) bands. The antenna proposed is successfully simulated and designed, which will satisfy the fundamental condition including widely frequency band match, stably antenna patterns.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Isoflux Radiation Antenna by Using Thin Dielectric Ring Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a simple thin dielectric-loaded lens antenna exhibiting an isoflux radiation pattern. The proposed antenna comprises a dielectric ring structure and a linear-to-circular polarizer structure, driven by a horn structure. The polarizer structure is integrated at the aperture plane of the horn, with the dielectric ring lens structure positioned above. Experimental results demonstrate successful isoflux beam radiation, with a maximum gain of approximately 7.15 dBic observed at a 25-degree angle from the boresight direction across the frequency range of 26 GHz to 36 GHz. The dielectric height is maintained at about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.07 \lambda_{0}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> denotes the wavelength of the central frequency.
