Additionally, within the operational frequency band, the antenna demonstrates a satisfactory axial ratio (AR) beamwidth. The antenna design is characterized by its simplicity and cost-effective fabrication.

articleTitle: Design of A 110-GHz On-Chip Antenna-Coupled Power-Adjustable Tripler based on Schottky Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of a 110-GHz on-chip antenna-coupled power-adjustable tripler based on the Schottky diodes. The design integrates two frequency triplers, on-chip antenna, and power synthesizing circuit on one single substrate. The input Ka-band signal is evenly divided via a power splitter into two signals, whose phase difference is adjusted with a phase shifter. Those two Schottky-diodes-tripled signals are synthesized by a 3-dB 90° coupler, and the output power is controllable by adjusting the phase difference between two signals after the power splitter. The simulation results show that the output power can be adjusted from -5 dBm to 17.67 dBm across - 25° to 85° phase difference range.

articleTitle: A 24-27GHz High Linearity LNA in 40nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a high linearity low noise amplifier (LNA) targeting for millimeter-wave 5G communication and radar applications. The LNA comprises two common-source (CS) stages, and the simulation results demonstrate that CS LNA can achieve high linearity. A LC inter-stage resonance matching network is used to improve in-band gain flatness. Additionally, the cut-off frequency of the transistors is analyzed and provides an accurate basis for the parameters used in the design. The post layout simulations from 23.5-28.5 GHz show a minimum gain of 12.8 dB, a maximum input and output reflection of -16.8 dB and -12.4 dB, respectively, 5.8 dB maximum NF, while IP1 is -4.2 dBm at 25.5 GHz under 50.8 mW DC power consumption using 1.1 V supply voltage. The chip size is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.336 \ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Advanced Electromagnetic Topology Optimization of Microstrip Line Filters Using Matrix Padé Via Lanczos (MPVL) Algorithm and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) topology optimization aims to optimize EM structures by manipulating materials within the design space. The genetic algorithm (GA) is commonly employed for such optimization tasks. This paper presents an efficient technique for EM topology optimization in microwave component design. It leverages the finite element method (FEM) for grid discretization and matrix equation extraction, integrating a novel formula derived from the Matrix Padé Via Lanczos(MPVL) iterative method and Householder method.

articleTitle: Design of Active Device for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces Based on Multi-Port Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have become a breakthrough technology with a wide range of applications because of their ability to manipulate electromagnetic (EM) waves. In this work, we present the design method of the active device for RISs based on a multi-port network. Initially, a multi-port network is employed to establish a surrogate model that offers reduced time and computational costs, serving as a viable surrogate to the EM model. Subsequently, genetic algorithm is implemented to optimize the passive structure of the RIS element. Finally, active devices are designed based on the optimized passive structure and their equivalent models, optimizing the performance of the RIS element. The performance of the proposed method is verified using a 2-bit phase-modulated RIS. Compared with EM model, this design method takes less time and does not require a lot of computation resources.

articleTitle: Research on Underground Space Signal Coverage Characteristics of Multi Band Wireless Ad Hoc Networks based on Ray Tracing Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In response to the high capacity requirements faced by wireless ad hoc networks in subway scenarios and the special impact of underground space environments, the main methods for studying the propagation characteristics of radio waves in enclosed space scenarios were first summarized. Then, the ray tracing method was applied to model and analyze the signal coverage characteristics of multi band wireless ad hoc networks in subway space scenarios. The calculation results can provide data support for optimizing the coverage of subway space wireless ad hoc network and verifying the effectiveness of the scheme.

articleTitle: A10-GHz Inductorless Type-II Sub-Sampling PLL with a Switched Loop Filter Achieving 127-fs RMS Jitter, −57.4-dBc Reference Spur and −266-dB FOMN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This article presents a 10-GHz sub-sampling type-II phase-locked loop (PLL) based on a ring oscillator. A switched loop filter is utilized to simultaneously achieve the low jitter and low spur without compromising the jitter-power trade-off. In addition, a low-power edge combiner is used to boost the output frequency from 2GHz to 10GHz. With a 100 MHz input sinewave reference, the proposed PLL in 28 nm CMOS achieves a spur level of −57.4dBc, a FOM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> of −266.3dB and an RMS jitter of 127fs integrated from 1k to 100MHz. The total power is 14.51mW at 10GHz, and the active area is 0.08mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A High-gain Antenna with Pattern and Polarization Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain F -P resonant cavity antenna with pattern and polarization reconfigurability is proposed. The antenna is formed by using the lower slot antenna as the radiation source and loading PRS on the upper layer. Through the simulation and processing experiments of the antenna, it is found that the proposed high-gain F -P resonant cavity antenna can reconstruct the directional pattern and polarization separately. The gain values of the antenna in various modes are greater than 11.5dBi. In addition, the main beam angle of the antenna can be adjusted from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi=0^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi=315^{\circ}$</tex> rotate at an angle of every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45^{\circ}$</tex> to complete beam reconstruction. The antenna has many advantages such as high gain, high efficiency, and simultaneous polarization pattern reconstruction, and has a wide range of applications in wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Profile Conformal Antenna in L Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Airborne platform growth makes new demands on antenna designing with the fast development of wireless technology. In this paper, a low-profile stealth monopole antenna is proposed, which can be widely used in airborne platform. Lightweight and corrosion resisting are important advantages. The results of simulation indicate that the antenna achieves 24% bandwidth subject to VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 2.5$</tex>. Gain of the antenna is no less than −2.5dBi, covering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$360^{\circ}\text{in}$</tex> azimuth plane and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$60^{\circ}\text{to}90^{\circ}\text{in}$</tex> elevation plane (normal direction of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}$</tex>). Measured results are presented, showing good agreement with simulation.

articleTitle: A $\text{94.4fs}_{rms}$ Cryogenic Sub-Sampling PLL in 4K for Quantum Computing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a fractional-N sub-sampling PLL (SSPLL) for cryogenic frequency source of in the quantum meas-urement and controller system. The proposed SSPLL adopts a 5-bit vector modulator (VM) based phase-interpolator (PI) and a 5-bit digital-to-time converter (DTC) for in-band phase noise sup-pression. According to the measured result, the SSPLL spans from 11.4GHz to 13.8GHz in 4K. When the SSPLL is divided by two, the output frequency is 6.3GHz. The measured RMS jitter is 94.37fs, the phase noise is -113.72dBc/Hz@100kHz, and the figure-of-the-merit (FoM) of -245.9dB is achieved.

articleTitle: A 9 pJ/b Ultra-Low Power MEMS-based OOK Transmitter in ISM-915 MHz Band for Pico-IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: An ISM 915-MHz OOK transmitter using MEMS resonator is presented. To achieve better power efficient, a cross-coupled RF oscillator using MEMS resonator is designed for the proposed OOK transmitter (TX) to generate the carrier frequency. The TX is implemented in a 65 nm CMOS technology, it delivers -16.6-dBm output power and consumes 0.54 mW power at I-V supply. Co-designed with a high-Q MEMS resonator, the phase noise of the TX is -128.3-dBc/Hz @ 100-kHz offset. The data rate of the TX could up to 60-Mb/s of OOK modulation when the driver amplifier is switched on or off directly, the energy efficiency is as low as 9 pJ/b.

articleTitle: Compact Band-Pass Filtering Antennas enabled with Mixed Electric and Magnetic Couplings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes the design method of utilizing mixed couplings theory between resonators with various antenna validations presented and discussed. Due to the mixed couplings excited between resonators, transmission zeros can be accomplished due to the existing 180° phase difference. An equivalent circuit analysis has been introduced here to demonstrate that the position of these transmission zeros can be shifted by adjusting the structures based on the principles of mixed-coupling theory. Based on the theoretical analysis, various antennas, including dipole and slot antennas, have been proposed here to demonstrate the design method. It is demonstrated that the proposed antennas have good band-pass filtering response with compact size.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Profile Circularly-Polarized Patch Filtenna Based on Dual-Mode SIW Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile circularly polarized (CP) patch filtenna based on dual-mode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity. This cavity works in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">120</inf> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{210}$</tex> modes, serving as the first-order resonator of the filtering structure and feeding four patches operating in the TM10 and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> modes at the same time. To achieve optimal axial ratio (AR) performance, we introduce two asymmetric posts within the SIW cavity, perturbing the distributions of electric field in two cavity modes. The CP performance is further improved after exciting four orthogonal patches vertically stacked in sequence by square slots employed on the cavity's top ground, achieving another AR minimum. Additionally, we employ four metallic posts penetrating the cavity to enhance impedance matching. To validate the feasibility of the proposed CP filtenna, a prototype (center frequency of 5.13GHz) is manufactured and experimented. The measured results closely match simulations, showing an impedance bandwidth of 6.9% (4.95-5.3GHz), a peak realized gain of 8.4 dBi, and a 3dB AR bandwidth of 4.2% (5-5.21GHz).

articleTitle: Research on Self-Excitation Phenomena of Millimeter Wave Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper finds the self-excitation of an amplifier and also gives the conditions of producing the self-excitation. As verified by the research and simulation analysis on the amplifier self-excitation, the contribution can provide some reference for avoiding self-excitation.
